articles.title: Is the Kennedy Center losing 'hundreds of millions of dollars'?
articles.summary: Records in 2024 show the venue had a surplus of millions of dollars once  contributions and grants had been factored in.
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has claimed the Kennedy Center in Washington DC has been losing "tens of millions of dollars, even hundreds of millions of dollars" for years.

Trump, who wants his name on the famous performing arts venue, was photographed onboard Air Force One looking at a poster with a headline that appeared to tout the demolition of the site.

articles.title: The best base layers and thermal underwear for surviving winter without overheating
articles.summary: The best thermal underwear includes  tops, bottoms and accessories from Smartwool, Patagonia, Backcountry and more.
articles.body: Whether you’re into snow sports or simply want to prepare for winter weather, base layers can help insulate heat while wicking sweat away from your skin. Those base layers can include thermal underwear, also known as long johns, as well as other types of apparel like shirts and accessories. Below you’ll find everything you need to know about base layers, including tips on how to shop for them, from Ashleigh McClary, a hiking enthusiast and Backcountry "Gearhead" (outdoor expert and customer service specialist), and Ben Clower, an outdoor enthusiast and marketing coordinator at JAX Outdoor Gear in Colorado. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best thermal underwear in 2026 The list below includes expert recommendations and some personal favorites of NBC Selected staff. Editor’s pick Former NBC Selected commerce editor Jordan Bowman loves these affordable Uniqlo tights for their flexible stretch and wide size range. In fact, he says he can’t survive a winter without them. “These are a necessity when temperatures drop in New York City,” he says. “If I see a gust of wind, that’s when I start reaching for the Heattech tights.” The tights are sleek and fitted for easy layering, and anti-odor, according to the brand. They’re designed to last through everyday wear and tear and hold their shape over time, according to the brand. Best men’s pants These 100% Merino wool bottoms from Smartwool come recommended by Clower. They have a slim fit that hugs the body and a mid-rise waistband designed to sit just at or below the belly button, according to the brand. To help reduce sagging, they also have a curved back seam for added support. To wash, the brand recommends a warm water, gentle cycle and drying on a low tumble. These bottoms are available in both men and women’s versions along with plus-size options up to 4X. Best men’s shirt Another recommendation from Clower, this crewneck thermal shirt is the matching top to the Smartwool bottoms on this list. Like the bottoms, this top has a slim fit and is made from the naturally odor-reducing Merino wool, according to the brand. The top has a flatlock seam, which is used in outdoor gear to reduce chafing, and shoulder panels instead of seams for a smoother look. Like the bottoms, this top is available in men and women’s sizing. Best splurge pick For people with sensitive skin who find Merino wool too itchy, McClary suggests Patagonia’s “incredibly soft and comfortable” Capilene Thermal base layers as an alternative. The fabric is Polartec Power Grid fleece, a mid- to lightweight base layer material designed to keep you warm without overheating your body, according to the brand. This hoodie has a regular fit, meaning it’s slightly looser than a fitted top, and can be layered with other pieces. Best women’s pant These are McClary’s favorite bottoms from the Patagonia Capilene line. They’re flexible and breathable, making them great for high-intensity activities like snowboarding, skiing, hiking and more. They have a reinforced crotch area to better allow for unrestricted movement, and flat seams to prevent chafing, according to the brand. Best women’s shirt This Merino wool half-zip top from Icebreaker is great for layering during extra-cold days, or for more active winter hobbies. It’s soft and lightweight, with design features like a reinforced underarm to allow for greater mobility, and offset shoulder seams to help minimize friction, according to the brand. The top has a slim, body-hugging fit for easy layering. Best lightweight women’s pant These base layer leggings are a favorite of former NBC Selected associate reporter Bianca Alvarez, who wears them for winter activities like snow tubing and skiing. “I love that they keep me warm but not to the point of overheating,” she says. She also likes the mesh calf design, which she says “makes the super soft material very breathable”, and how the long cuffs are comfortable to wear, even with snow boots. Best budget pick Alvarez says that since her mom first bought these tops on a Costco run, her entire family wears them regularly as base layers under their winter clothes. Initially, she thought they were too thin to be effective, but says that after trying the top, she was happily wrong. “These are one of the warmest thermal layers I own,” she says. “I wear it on its own, under vests and of course, under winter jackets.” She also likes that the top is available in packs of two, and is machine washable. “It feels softer and softer after every wash,” she says. Best lightweight men’s long underwear These long underwear are soft and stretchy to allow for less restrictive movement, according to the brand. They’re made from a poly-spandex blend that gives them a flexible feel, and are also designed with a sweat-wicking Thermaskin technology to keep your skin dry while wearing. The full elastic waistband keeps the thermal underwear in place, while the fabric has odor-controlling properties to keep you fresh at all times. These long underwear are available in both regular and tall sizes. Best thermal set This thermal underwear set is designed to be an everyday base layer, according to the brand. Each piece is lined with fleece for extra softness, and the set is highly rated by reviewers on Amazon. The top is available in scoop neck, crew neck and V-neck styles, and both pieces can also be worn without a top layer. Best active top If you’re looking for a workout-friendly thermal base layer, consider this option from Baleaf. This top is fleece-lined for added warmth, and has thumb holes to keep your sleeves in place while doing intense movement, according to the brand. The fabric is light enough to prevent overheating while wearing, and also has reflective elements to help with visibility during cold weather activities in the dark. The top also has a side zip-up pocket for added convenience. The best thermal accessories “Your search for warm base layers shouldn’t be limited to just tops and bottoms,” says McClary. Thermal accessories can provide insulation and warmth for your head, hands and more — below, I rounded up some of the best thermal accessories, including expert picks and highly-rated options from top retailers. How I picked the best thermal underwear Per expert guidance, I kept the following in mind while pulling together our list: Types: To make this list as comprehensive as possible, I included base layers of all different kinds, including tops, bottoms and accessories.Material: Clower calls Merino wool “the ultimate material” for thermal underwear because of its heat-trapping and temperature-regulating properties. For shoppers who find wool itchy, alternative (synthetic) fabrics like polyester, nylon and spandex offer the best value and good performance — certain blends of these materials, according to McClary, are just as warm as Merino wool. However, if you choose Merino wool, be sure to check the underwear’s temperature rating to be sure that it fits your needs (more on that below). The list below includes both 100% Merino wool and synthetic blend options, so you can find the best choice for your needs. How to shop for thermal underwear As you shop for your own thermal underwear, there are a few things you should keep in mind, including the underwear’s fabric weight and, when it comes to Merino wool, the temperature rating. Fabric weight: According to McClary, not all thermal underwear is the same warmth level, which is why she always checks the weight/density of the fabric before buying. “I look for keywords like lightweight, midweight, heavyweight or thermal weight,” she says. Lightweight options are best for cooler temperatures, whereas midweight thermal underwear works well with moderately cold weather. However in cases where a lot of extra warmth is needed, like below-zero temperatures, heavyweight underwear are best. Temperature rating: If you opt for Merino wool underwear, the temperature rating is a key factor. “Temperature rating is important because you want the appropriate amount of warmth for the temperatures you expect,” says Clower. The temperature rating corresponds with the fabric weight of Merino wool, which is measured in grams per square meter (GSM), according to the experts. McClary says she considers anything with a GSM of 100 or less to be lightweight warmth, anything from 100-250 GSM to be midweight warmth, and any thermal underwear with a GSM of 250 or higher to be heavyweight warmth. articles.title: Plumbers share the sink accessories that stop food scraps from becoming an expensive problem
articles.summary: One is a surprisingly simple, inexpensive buy that you may already have hiding in your cabinet.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

You probably don't think too much about what's going on below your kitchen sink — at least until you're standing there, waiting for the water to slowly drain. Clogs have definitely left me staring at a pool of murky dishwater, wondering how a few crumbs here and there turned into what feels like a plumbing emergency.

Depending on the situation, your clogged sink might be a mere inconvenience or a much more costly problem. The good news is that preventing a clogged kitchen sink doesn't require anything particularly complicated, and some savvy habits and smart buys could head off a steep plumbing bill.

I'm guilty of leaving my sink strainer sitting on the counter because it's gross to empty, or I keep it out of sight because it's not the most aesthetically pleasing thing. After all, I have a garbage disposal, so if a few things slip down the drain, I'm not too concerned.

Well, plumbers have a message for me: Put the strainer back where it belongs. A simple strainer catches food scraps before they enter your drainage system, says Mike Winklejohn, a licensed journeyman plumber and regional operations manager at HomeServe . Plus it's easy to lift out, empty into the trash and put back in the sink.

Paul Abrams, a spokesperson for Roto-Rooter , agrees that a basket strainer is one of the simplest, most useful tools for preventing clogs. Many kitchen sinks come with one but plenty of homeowners, like me, don't actually use them. But you're not just stuck with the one you got by default; there are several different types, including deep-basket strainers, flexible mesh baskets, hanging sink baskets and disposable strainers. All can help make collecting food scraps and dumping them in the trash a little easier. If wet food in the sink makes you a little green, a strainer basket or a disposable option might be the better choice. Otherwise, a traditional strainer works just fine.

Of course, a strainer shouldn't be your only line of defense. Abrams recommends scraping leftover food off your plate and into the trash before rinsing, then letting the strainer catch whatever small bits remain.

Doncko Disposable Mesh Sink Strainers, 400-Pack

Sdefi Stainless Steel Kitchen Sink Drain Strainer

Use a garbage disposal — but don't treat it like a trash can

I have a garbage disposal, and it certainly makes kitchen cleanup a little easier when I'm dealing with small bits of food stuck to dishes and pans. But I'm terrified of putting anything bigger than a crumb down it. (I learned my lesson in the past, when I clogged the other side of my sink.)

Garbage disposals are probably the most popular sink accessory for preventing large food scraps from becoming a plumbing problem, Winklejohn says. And you've got plenty of options to choose from, depending on how finely you want one to grind your food, how quiet you want it to be and how long you want it to last (stainless steel is a better option for preventing rust).

But even the fanciest disposal can't make every food scrap disappear without consequence. "The best practice is to scrape food into the trash before rinsing dishes," Abrams says. A garbage disposal is meant to handle small food scraps left behind, not a sink full of last night's leftovers. Abrams also cautions that you shouldn't wait until the disposal is packed with food before turning it on, which can lead to clogs.

And there's another golden rule both pros agree on: Run cold water when the disposal is on, since it helps solidify any grease that's gone down the drain and makes it easier for the blades to break it up. (For years, I've been running hot water down my disposal, thinking it would break up any residue left behind — live and learn.) Abrams also says to leave the water running for at least 10 seconds after you shut off the disposal to ensure the ground-up waste is flushed through the drainpipe.

Waste Maid 1/2 HP Anti-Jam Garbage Disposal

Moen Prep Series Pro 1/2 HP Garbage Disposal

InSinkErator Badger 5 1/2 HP Garbage Disposal

Stop putting these foods down the disposal and drain

To me, the name "garbage disposal" feels a little misleading — especially if you're a first-time owner. You might think you can just shove an uneaten pile of pasta down it, but that's not the case. And the same goes for your sink drain. Abrams says the list of no-nos, whether or not you have a disposal, includes rice, pasta, potato peels, mashed potatoes, coffee grounds, eggshells, bones, seeds, poultry skin, pumpkin pulp, citrus peels, corn husks, meat drippings, cooking oil and grease.

Starchy foods are particularly troublesome because they can break down into a sticky paste that coats pipes and traps other debris — think of the residue left on your hands after cutting potatoes. But that doesn't mean you need to panic if a few grains of rice slip down. "Your disposal can process small amounts of these items, so there is no need to be paranoid, but your motto should be, 'All things in moderation,'" Abrams says.

Both experts are especially firm on this rule: Never pour grease or cooking oil down the sink. Grease can solidify in the drainage system, causing clogs, Winklejohn says. I personally wait for it to solidify and then scrape it into the trash, or pour hot oil into a silicone grease catcher. You can also use a cooking oil solidifier on hot oil, and once it's cooled down, scrape it right into the trash.

A small countertop compost bin is another option for larger food scraps. It's a great way to keep foul smells from festering in the garbage and protect your drain. Just make sure you're emptying the bin regularly to keep pests and unwanted odors at bay.

PrepSolutions Silicone Grease Strainer and Keeper

LaSyL Natural Cooking Oil Solidifier Powder

Sink already clogged? Don't make matters worse

If you're already dealing with a sink full of dingy water, it happens to the best of us. But before you reach for harsh chemical drain cleaners, here are a few tips to try first.

If you have a garbage disposal, run it to see if the clog clears. Next, try a short-handled sink plunger (and please don't grab the toilet plunger you keep in your bathroom). Abrams advises making sure there's enough water in the sink to cover the plunger. You should also seal any overflow openings, then cover the drain on the opposite side if you have a double sink. Next, give it six to 10 firm plunges, then repeat as needed. "Ideally, the pressure from the plunger will break up the clog and force it through the drainpipe," he notes.

You can also try baking soda and vinegar, but Abrams says the mixture is generally not effective on a complete blockage. Boiling water isn't always the miracle cure it's made out to be either. If there's already standing water in the sink, it probably won't do much to clear the clog. Plus, Abrams notes that it can warp acrylic sink tubs and crack some natural stone sinks, which can lead to another very expensive problem.

As for chemical drain openers like Drano, Abrams says they may work in some situations, but they can also damage pipes and drain finishes. And if you've already poured chemicals down the drain and your next step is to call a plumber, Abrams says you need to let them know so they can take the proper safety precautions.

If you're dealing with a truly stubborn clog, you may need to grab a bucket, place it under the sink and do a little investigation. Abrams says homeowners can start by removing the P-trap — it looks like a U- or P-shaped pipe and it connects your sink's drain to the sewer system or septic tank — to check for debris. This isn't for those who have a weak stomach, especially if the clog has been there for days.

If the P-trap is clear, Abrams says you can try a hand-crank drain auger (a plumbing snake), but advises against using powered augers if you don't have training. If the clog is beyond the reach of a household auger, it's time for the pros to take over. Let them know what you've already taken apart so they can check that everything was reassembled correctly.

articles.title: Do elections in Russia make a difference?
articles.summary: Millions of people are choosing a new lower house of Parliament.
articles.body:
Critics say the outcome of the elections in Russia is a foregone conclusion. Millions of people are eligible to choose a new State Duma, or lower house of Parliament.

This is the first vote since Russia invaded Ukraine in February 2022. And there’s no doubt the war is overshadowing this process.

The cost of living has increased, and Ukrainian drones are increasingly targeting oil refineries and warehouses.

President Vladimir Putin has urged voters to cast their ballots in a show of support for the military. But what leverage, if any, does the State Duma have in Russia’s politics?

articles.title: Artesanato indígena da Amazônia é destaque em feira de Paris | G1
articles.standfirst: Produção brasileira foi selecionada entre mais de 600 inscritos para uma agenda de negócios em Paris e chegou a uma das principais feiras europeias de design de interiores.
articles.summary: O artesanato indígena da Amazônia chegou à Maison&Objet em Paris, destacando a arte indígena brasileira no mercado internacional de design de interiores.
articles.body:
Artesanato indígena da Amazônia ganha espaço em feira internacional de design em Paris — Foto: Foto: Divulgação

De territórios indígenas da Amazônia para uma das principais vitrines internacionais de design e decoração. Em setembro, peças produzidas por povos indígenas brasileiros chegaram a Paris, na França, onde foram apresentadas a compradores, lojistas e profissionais de diferentes países durante uma agenda voltada à inserção do artesanato brasileiro no mercado internacional.

A movimentação fez parte da segunda edição da Jornada Exportadora do Artesanato, promovida pela Agência Brasileira de Promoção de Exportações e Investimentos (ApexBrasil). Entre mais de 600 negócios inscritos, 20 empresas, associações e cooperativas foram selecionadas para participar da programação, que incluiu seminários sobre os mercados francês e europeu, visitas técnicas e rodadas de negócios com compradores internacionais.

Entre as selecionadas estava a Tucum Brasil, plataforma especializada na comercialização de arte indígena brasileira e integrante do portfólio da AMAZ Aceleradora. A iniciativa é coordenada pelo Idesam – Instituto de Conservação e Desenvolvimento da Amazônia, organização que atua com práticas sustentáveis e inovação em bioeconomia na Amazônia, trabalhando com comunidades tradicionais, negócios e organizações para fortalecer redes produtivas e conectar diferentes atores do ecossistema de impacto.

Além da participação na Jornada Exportadora, a Tucum foi uma das 10 iniciativas escolhidas para expor produtos na Maison&Objet, uma importante feira francesa de design de interiores realizada semestralmente em Paris e considerada um dos principais eventos europeus do setor. A empresa integrou a exposição “Brasil Nostálgic”, com produtos selecionados pelo curador Bruno Simões, no estande da ApexBrasil.

A participação colocou peças produzidas por povos indígenas brasileiros em contato com profissionais e compradores ligados aos mercados de design, decoração e objetos. Para a Tucum, a experiência também serviu para entender melhor as oportunidades e os desafios de levar essa produção para outros países.

Segundo a fundadora e gestora da Tucum, Amanda Santana, a empresa teve contato com mais de 15 potenciais compradores e lojistas durante a programação. Entre eles estavam representantes da França, Grécia, Islândia, Reino Unido e Bélgica, além de brasileiros que mantêm negócios na Europa.

“Foi uma oportunidade tanto para a Tucum estabelecer contato e, de repente, fechar negócios em maior escala com esses compradores quanto para aprender também”, afirma Amanda.

Da floresta para o mercado internacional

Levar uma peça produzida em uma comunidade indígena até um comprador em outro país envolve mais do que encontrar um mercado interessado. O processo passa pelo tempo de produção, pela dinâmica das comunidades, pela formação dos preços e pela logística necessária para retirar os produtos de territórios muitas vezes distantes dos grandes centros.

Esse é um dos pontos que a Tucum tem buscado apresentar aos compradores internacionais. Segundo Amanda, o artesanato indígena não segue necessariamente uma lógica de produção contínua ou em escala. A confecção das peças acontece de acordo com a rotina de cada comunidade e é conciliada com outras atividades do cotidiano.

“Esse fazer acontece em determinados momentos que são separados para isso. Isso implica também na forma como a gente escala e na forma como a gente forma o preço”, explica.

A distância entre os territórios de origem e os mercados consumidores também pesa. Produtos produzidos em áreas remotas da Amazônia precisam percorrer diferentes etapas até chegar a cidades como Manaus ou Rio de Janeiro e, posteriormente, seguir para outros países.

“Temos a complexa logística de retirar um produto de dentro da floresta para chegar ao Rio de Janeiro ou chegar em Manaus e depois ser despachado para outro país, em outra parte do mundo”, relata.

Nesse cenário, a internacionalização não envolve apenas encontrar compradores, mas também criar condições para que a comercialização considere o modo de produção das comunidades e seja viável para quem está na origem das peças.

A presença na Maison&Objet marcou a primeira participação da Tucum na feira. A empresa foi selecionada para integrar a exposição “Brasil Nostálgic”, no estande da ApexBrasil, com produtos escolhidos pelo curador Bruno Simões.

Para Amanda, a experiência abriu uma frente diferente das rodadas tradicionais de negócios ao colocar as peças em um ambiente frequentado por profissionais ligados ao design e à decoração.

“Foi a primeira vez que a gente participou de uma feira dessas. Achei muito importante para a gente colocar o nosso produto nesse circuito”, afirma.

A Tucum também recebeu uma Bolsa Exportação da ApexBrasil, no valor de R$ 20 mil, destinada a auxiliar a participação da empresa em outros eventos de promoção comercial organizados pela agência.

A delegação da Jornada Exportadora do Artesanato reuniu 20 empresas, associações e cooperativas selecionadas entre mais de 600 inscrições. Segundo Amanda, 95% dos participantes eram mulheres.

A Tucum foi fundada em 2013, no Rio de Janeiro, inicialmente como uma loja física. Em 2015, passou a atuar como marketplace de arte indígena, reunindo produtos de diferentes povos e territórios.

Atualmente, a empresa atua em quatro Unidades de Conservação e 56 Terras Indígenas distribuídas por oito estados da Amazônia Legal. A rede reúne associações, cooperativas, grupos e artistas indígenas.

Entre os produtos comercializados estão roupas, bolsas, biojoias, peças de artesanato, pinturas e objetos de decoração. Em 2024, a Tucum comprou R$ 538 mil em mercadorias, beneficiando artesãos e artesãs de 106 povos indígenas que vivem em 62 territórios tradicionais. Entre os povos parceiros estão Baniwa, Baré, Guarani, Kayapó, Ticuna e Yanomami.

A participação na Jornada Exportadora não foi a primeira experiência internacional da empresa. Em 2025, a Tucum integrou a edição realizada em Lisboa, em Portugal. Para Amanda, voltar ao programa um ano depois permitiu comparar as experiências e chegar a Paris com novos aprendizados.

“Eu tenho certeza que ter participado dessa segunda jornada trouxe mais aprendizados e que a gente também teve contato com mais compradores, compradores mais qualificados. Acho que vão surgir bons negócios”, avalia.

Para a fundadora, ampliar o acesso a mercados também pode aumentar as possibilidades de geração de renda para as comunidades produtoras.

“Na nossa missão de valorizar e promover as artes indígenas do Brasil, a Tucum vê na exportação uma oportunidade de gerar mais renda e impactos positivos para as artistas que mantêm seu território com a floresta de pé”, afirma.

A Tucum integra o portfólio da AMAZ Aceleradora, iniciativa coordenada pelo Idesam. O Instituto de Conservação e Desenvolvimento da Amazônia também é parceiro da Fundação Rede Amazônica em iniciativas voltadas ao desenvolvimento sustentável e à valorização de soluções para a Amazônia.

articles.title: Previsão do tempo em Alagoas: chuva e calor de 33°C no fim de semana | G1
articles.standfirst: Semarh prevê chuva passageira principalmente em Maceió, no Litoral e na Zona da Mata. Sertão pode registrar temperaturas de até 33°C.
articles.summary: A previsão do tempo em Alagoas indica chuvas passageiras em Maceió e no Litoral, enquanto o Sertão deve registrar calor de até 33°C neste fim de semana.
articles.body:
Chuvas em Alagoas. — Foto: Victoria Alcântara

O fim de semana deve ter chuva passageira em diferentes regiões de Alagoas, segundo a previsão da Secretaria de Estado do Meio Ambiente e dos Recursos Hídricos (Semarh).

Maceió , Litoral e Zona da Mata estão entre as áreas com maior possibilidade de chuva. Já o Sertão deve ter tempo mais firme e temperaturas de até 33°C.

articles.standfirst: Hóspede usa e vai embora, e o desgaste fica. Veja como escolher equipamento de área de lazer que aguenta rotatividade e não vira manutenção
articles.summary: Hóspede usa e vai embora, e o desgaste fica. Veja como escolher equipamento de área de lazer que aguenta rotatividade e não vira manutenção
articles.body:
Quem coloca a casa de campo em aluguel por temporada descobre rápido que equipamento de uso doméstico não aguenta rotatividade . Cada grupo usa de um jeito, ninguém tem o cuidado de dono, e o que era detalhe vira manutenção recorrente. Escolher o que fica na casa é uma decisão econômica, não de gosto.

Kits de churrasqueira com rodas: equipamento móvel e resistente para locação — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

•Antiaderente: hóspede usa garfo de metal e a camada vai em um fim de semana.

•Peça de plástico e cabo colado: solta, derrete, quebra.

•Grelha fina: empena no primeiro carvão além da conta.

•Equipamento fixo em área descoberta: acumula chuva e corrói entre as locações.

Equipamento de uso doméstico não aguenta rotatividade: hóspede não tem o cuidado de dono.

O que funciona em casa alugada é o oposto do que se escolhe para uso próprio: robustez acima de refinamento . Peça de ferro ou aço espesso, sem revestimento para arruinar, sem componente frágil e — importante — guardável . Equipamento que se recolhe entre as locações não sofre chuva nem desaparece.

1.P refira s em revestimento: ferro e aço não têm camada para o hóspede estragar.

2.E scolha m óvel com rodas: recolher entre locações preserva e evita furto.

3.E vite peça de uso único; hóspede usa o que é óbvio.

4.T enha r eposição barata do que inevitavelmente se perde (utensílios, tampas).

5.D eixe instrução simples de uso e limpeza à vista.

Sediada em Divinópolis , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, a Panela de Ferro Fundido trabalha com churrasqueiras e kits para área de lazer. Os modelos estão no catálogo de kits de churrasqueira , com entrega para todo o Brasil.

articles.title: El Niño e calor intenso: Veja como reduzir o consumo de energia | G1
articles.standfirst: Com os efeitos do El Niño, a adoção de hábitos conscientes ajuda a evitar surpresas na conta de energia ao final do mês
articles.summary: Com os efeitos do El Niño, a adoção de hábitos conscientes ajuda a evitar surpresas na conta de energia ao final do mês
articles.body:
Com os efeitos do El Niño, a adoção de hábitos conscientes ajuda a evitar surpresas na conta de energia ao final do mês — Foto: Divulgação

Você já percebeu como os dias têm ficado cada vez mais quentes? Além das altas temperaturas deste período, a influência do El Niño contribui para um calor ainda mais intenso, o que impacta diretamente no uso da energia elétrica.

Com isso, equipamentos de refrigeração, como ar-condicionado e ventiladores, permanecem ligados por mais tempo, aumentando o gasto de eletricidade nas residências.

A analista de Eficiência Energética da Energisa Acre, Asmiliane Fernandes, reforça que atitudes simples podem fazer uma diferença significativa no fim do mês.

"Pequenas práticas no dia a dia ajudam a manter o uso da energia equilibrado sem abrir mão do conforto. Apagar as luzes de ambientes vazios, desligar aparelhos quando não estiverem em uso e optar por equipamentos mais eficientes são algumas delas. No caso dos ventiladores, é importante lembrar que eles proporcionam sensação de conforto térmico, mas não resfriam o ambiente. Por isso, devem ser desligados quando não houver ninguém no local" , afirma Asmiliane.

A analista reforça ainda que ajustar o ar-condicionado para temperaturas muito baixas não significa que o ambiente ficará mais gelado com mais rapidez.

"Mesmo que o ar esteja em 16°, ele nunca vai chegar nessa temperatura por conta do calor do lado de fora. O equipamento vai trabalhar muito (como a geladeira e bebedouro também, por exemplo), consumir ainda mais energia e deixar a conta mais cara no fim do mês", explica.

•Stand-by: r etire da tomada os aparelhos que não estão sendo utilizados, pois eles continuam consumindo energia mesmo quando parecem desligados.

•Lâmpadas: s ubstitua as convencionais por modelos LED, que consomem até 80% menos energia do que as incandescentes e fluorescentes.

•Geladeira: evite abrir a porta sem necessidade, verifique a borracha de vedação e não coloque alimentos quentes nem encostados no fundo do equipamento e nem deixe o equipamento próximo do fogão.

•Ferro e máquina de lavar: acumule as roupas para passar e lavar tudo de uma só vez.

•Ventilador: mantenha portas e janelas abertas para melhorar a circulação do ar e aumentar a sensação de frescor. Desligue o equipamento quando o ambiente estiver vazio.

•Ar-condicionado: utilize-o preferencialmente na temperatura de 23°C. Faça a limpeza periódica dos filtros e mantenha as manutenções em dia.

•Carregadores: retire celulares e notebooks da tomada após o carregamento completo.

articles.title: Aeroporto de Natal tem maior movimento em agosto desde 2014 | G1
articles.standfirst: Terminal potiguar recebeu 242,6 mil passageiros em agosto. Movimento internacional cresceu 76% na comparação com o mesmo mês de 2025.
articles.summary: O Aeroporto de Natal registrou 242,6 mil passageiros em agosto, com alta de 76% em voos internacionais e recorde de movimentação sob nova gestão.
articles.body:
Passageiros de voo internacional no Aeroporto de Natal — Foto: Edu Rocha

O Aeroporto Internacional de Natal , localizado em São Gonçalo do Amarante, registrou em agosto o maior movimento de passageiros para o mês desde o início das operações, em 2014. Ao todo, foram 242,6 mil passageiros entre embarques e desembarques, alta de 21% em relação a agosto de 2025.

Do total registrado em agosto, 227,9 mil passageiros viajaram em voos domésticos, crescimento de 18% na comparação com o mesmo mês do ano passado. Já o movimento internacional somou 14,6 mil passageiros, alta de 76%. Os dados são da Zurich Airport Brasil, administradora do terminal.

Agosto foi o quarto mês de 2026 em que o aeroporto apresentou crescimento superior a 20% no fluxo de passageiros. O mês de julho também registrou o maior movimento para o período desde a inauguração do aeroporto.

De acordo com a Zurich, nos meses de julho e agosto, São Paulo, Brasília, Rio de Janeiro, Buenos Aires e Lisboa estiveram entre os principais mercados emissores de passageiros para o Aeroporto de Natal.

No primeiro semestre de 2026, o Aeroporto de Natal recebeu 1.387.440 passageiros, entre embarques e desembarques. O número representa um crescimento de 18% em relação ao mesmo período de 2025 e o melhor resultado para os seis primeiros meses do ano desde a inauguração do terminal.

Segundo dados da Agência Nacional de Aviação Civil (Anac), o movimento também foi o maior registrado em um aeroporto do Rio Grande do Norte no primeiro semestre desde 2002.

Atualmente, o Aeroporto de Natal oferece voos diretos para 17 destinos nacionais e internacionais. A Azul anunciou novas rotas ligando Natal a Goiânia e Curitiba, com operações previstas entre dezembro de 2026 e janeiro de 2027.

A Latam também anunciou uma rota direta entre Natal e Buenos Aires a partir de dezembro. A capital argentina já é atendida pela Gol e pela JetSMART.

Desde que assumiu a administração do aeroporto, em fevereiro de 2024, a Zurich Airport Brasil afirma ter investido cerca de R$ 59 milhões na infraestrutura do terminal.

articles.summary: O leilão da Receita Federal em Teresina oferece veículos e eletrônicos com propostas abertas a partir do dia 21 de setembro pelo portal e-CAC.
articles.body:
A Receita Federal abre, na próxima segunda-feira (21), o prazo para envio de propostas do segundo leilão eletrônico — Foto: Imagem ilustrativa

A Receita Federal abre, na próxima segunda-feira (21), o prazo para envio de propostas do segundo leilão eletrônico de mercadorias e veículos de 2026. Em Teresina, os interessados poderão conferir presencialmente os produtos disponíveis para arrematação.

Ao todo, serão ofertados 411 lotes com itens como veículos, eletrônicos e materiais de informática . Os bens leiloados são produtos abandonados, entregues à Fazenda Nacional ou objeto de pena de perdimento em ações de fiscalização da Receita Federal.

As propostas poderão ser enviadas entre 8h do dia 21 de setembro e 21h do dia 25 de setembro, no horário de Brasília. A classificação e ordenação das propostas ocorrerão às 9h do dia 28 de setembro, enquanto a sessão pública de lances terá início às 10h da mesma data.

Em Teresina, a visitação dos produtos deverá ocorrer entre os dias 21 e 25 de setembro, mediante agendamento.

Um dos pontos de visitação informados pela Receita Federal fica na Rua João Cabral, nº 1607, no bairro Vermelha. Os horários e locais dos demais lotes podem ser consultados no edital do leilão .

Além de Teresina, as cidades de Fortaleza (CE), São Gonçalo do Amarante (CE) e São Luís (MA) também terão espaços destinados à realização da conferência dos produtos.

Para participar, os interessados devem acessar o Centro Virtual de Atendimento ao Contribuinte (e-CAC), por meio de uma conta Gov.br nos níveis Prata ou Ouro. O acesso ao edital e ao sistema de envio de propostas também é feito pelo portal da Receita Federal .

As sessões de lances poderão ser acompanhadas em tempo real pelo site da Receita Federal.

articles.standfirst: Movimento Antonietas, iniciativa da NSC voltada ao protagonismo e fortalecimento das mulheres catarinenses, está presente no Festival Social Good Brasil 2026, em Florianópolis.
articles.summary: No Festival Social Good Brasil, Eveline Poncio debate o empreendedorismo feminino no Brasil e o papel do Movimento Antonietas na inclusão produtiva de mulheres.
articles.body:
O Movimento Antonietas, iniciativa da NSC voltada ao protagonismo e fortalecimento das mulheres catarinenses, está presente no Festival Social Good Brasil 2026, nesta sexta-feira (18).

A jornalista Eveline Poncio, apresentadora do Bom Dia Santa Catarina, da NSC TV, media um painel sobre desafios e oportunidades das mulheres que empreendem por necessidade no Brasil.

O evento ocorre no Centro de Inovação ACATE Primavera, em Florianópolis, e reúne lideranças, especialistas e organizações que atuam na construção de soluções inovadoras para desafios sociais contemporâneos.

Nesta edição, o festival propõe o tema “Gingado: inovação brasileira em movimento”, destacando a capacidade do Brasil de transformar conhecimento coletivo, diversidade e criatividade em impacto social.

A programação busca conectar tecnologia, cultura e inovação a partir das múltiplas inteligências presentes em diferentes territórios e realidades do país.

“Quem são as mulheres que empreendem por necessidade no Brasil?”

Representando o Movimento Antonietas, Eveline modera o painel “Quem são as mulheres que empreendem por necessidade no Brasil?”, realizado das 16h às 17h30.

O debate, com participação do Instituto Consulado da Mulher e da ENGIE, apresenta histórias, dados e evidências sobre como a inclusão produtiva pode transformar vidas, ampliar a autonomia financeira e promover o desenvolvimento social.

O painel discute os desafios que ainda limitam o futuro de milhares de nanoempreendedoras brasileiras, reforçando a importância de iniciativas voltadas à geração de renda, capacitação e ampliação de oportunidades.

“Participar de um evento como o Social Good é uma oportunidade de ampliar o alcance de discussões fundamentais. O empreendedorismo feminino, especialmente aquele que nasce da necessidade, revela histórias de coragem, resiliência e inovação que merecem ser conhecidas e valorizadas”, destacou Eveline Poncio.

Criado pela NSC, o Movimento Antonietas reúne projetos, conteúdos e iniciativas voltados ao fortalecimento da presença feminina em diferentes setores da sociedade. Por meio da promoção de debates, conexões e ações de impacto social, o movimento busca ampliar oportunidades, dar visibilidade a trajetórias inspiradoras e contribuir para uma sociedade mais inclusiva e equitativa.

articles.title: Produção de milho em Rio Verde: cidade é a 2ª maior do Brasil | G1
articles.standfirst: Estado ocupa a segunda e a quarta posições entre os maiores produtores do Brasil. Área de milho plantado supera 300 mil hectares.
articles.summary: A produção de milho em Rio Verde cresceu 18,7% e atingiu 2,67 milhões de toneladas, consolidando Goiás como destaque no ranking do IBGE.
articles.body:
Trabalhador segura grãos de milho — Foto: Wildes Barbosa/O Popular

O município de Rio Verde , no sudoeste do estado, alcançou o 2º lugar no ranking nacional da produção de milho . Levantamento do Instituto Brasileiro de Geografia e Estatística (IBGE) mostra que, em 2025, a produção estimada do grão foi de 2,67 milhões de toneladas. O milho também ocupa a segunda posição em valor de produção, somando R$ 13,7 bilhões.

Segundo o levantamento, a produção de milho em Rio Verde aumentou 18,7% em relação a 2024 , quando foram produzidas 2,25 milhões de toneladas na cidade. O IBGE mostrou que a área destinada à colheita também cresceu, passando de 334,3 mil hectares em 2024 para 352,0 mil em 2025 (crescimento de 5,3%).

O levantamento mostra que Goiás ocupa posição de destaque em relação ao milho, com dois municípios entre os quatro maiores produtores do país. Na liderança nacional está a cidade de Sorriso, no Mato Grosso.

Em Goiás, além da 2ª colocação de Rio Verde, o estado tem Jataí na 4ª colocação do Brasil na produção do grão. A cidade deve alcançar 2,02 milhões de toneladas, aumento de 6,7% em relação a 2024, enquanto a área plantada avançou de 282,0 mil para 288,0 mil hectares, crescimento de 2,1%.

A produção de milho em todo o estado também é a maior já registrada , com a área plantada passando de 2,12 milhões de hectares para 2,37 milhões, crescimento de 11,6%. A produção saltou 24,6% e alcançou os 15,95 milhões de toneladas. Em 2024 a produção foi de 12,8 milhões de toneladas, registradas.

O milho ocupa a segunda posição estadual em valor de produção, com R$ 13,7 bilhões e crescimento de 42,1% em relação a 2024.

articles.title: Passageiros trocam socos durante voo de Bangladesh para Londres | G1
articles.standfirst: Briga de dois homens escalou para pancadaria em voo da Biman Bangladesh Airlines. Camiseta de um deles foi rasgada durante o confronto.
articles.summary: Dois passageiros brigaram durante um voo entre Bangladesh e Londres. Vídeo mostra os homens trocando socos antes de serem separados pela tripulação.
articles.body:
Dois passageiros entraram em uma briga feia durante um voo da companhia aérea Biman Bangladesh Airlines com destino a Londres, no Reino Unido . Imagens gravadas dentro do avião mostram os homens trocando socos e entrando em confronto enquanto outros passageiros tentavam separá-los.

A confusão aconteceu na última quinta-feira (17), durante um voo entre Sylhet, em Bangladesh , e a capital britânica. Segundo a companhia aérea, a briga começou após uma discussão entre os dois homens e terminou depois que a tripulação interveio.

Nas imagens, os homens aparecem agarrados e trocando golpes entre os assentos. A camiseta de um deles chegou a ser rasgada durante o confronto.

A confusão assustou outros passageiros que estavam no avião, incluindo crianças e idosos. O vídeo foi posteriormente publicado e compartilhado nas redes sociais.

Mohiuddin Ahmed, gerente-geral do departamento de relações públicas da Biman Bangladesh Airlines, confirmou ao Daily Mail que houve uma briga durante o voo.

Segundo ele, a tripulação conseguiu controlar a situação. A companhia não informou o motivo da discussão nem disse se algum dos passageiros ficou ferido.

Também não foi informado se os envolvidos sofreram alguma punição depois do pouso em Londres.

Vídeo mostra homens brigando entre os assentos; camiseta de um deles foi rasgada durante o confronto. Companhia aérea confirmou o caso. — Foto: Reprodução: Redes Sociais

articles.title: Forced adoption records could 'unlock' missing histories
articles.summary: A campaigner says church records could reveal the hidden history of forced-adoption homes.
articles.body:
A woman whose baby was taken from her in a forced adoption aged 16 has said important questions about the UK's mother-and-baby homes remain unanswered, including how many children were buried in unmarked graves.

Diana Defries, who successfully campaigned for a state apology for forced adoptions , said greater access to records could help families understand what happened in the homes.

And historian Dr Michael Lambert, from Lancaster University, argued that archives held privately by religious congregations could help "unlock" important pieces of history.

Defries, originally from London, was sent by her family to Nazareth House in Southampton in 1974 after becoming pregnant.

"I remember the feeling of walking into somewhere that would change me," she said.

The home, run by the Catholic Sisters of Nazareth, received funding from Southampton social services, as well as fees paid by the families of women who stayed there.

The mother-and-baby wing opened in 1960 and by the time it closed in 1985, local media reported it had housed 1,552 women and girls.

Unmarked graves of children who died in Nazareth Houses, which were then mostly a network of residential care facilities and orphanages run by the Sisters of Nazareth, and in similar institutions operated by other religious orders, have been found in the UK.

Sister Anna Maria Doolan, safeguarding lead for the Sisters of Nazareth, said the order welcomed and supported the government's apology for forced adoptions.

In a statement, Doolan said: "Requests to access information regarding former residents are welcome in line with the archive access policy.

"However, the records are sometimes, sadly, incomplete as the guidelines for keeping records pre-1980 were very different to today's requirements."

After giving birth in hospital and returning to the home, Defries said she was discouraged from holding her baby to prevent her from bonding.

It was only on the train to the adoption agency in London, accompanied by her mother, that she said she was able to really hold her daughter.

"I didn't want to let her go," she said.

"I kept holding on to the idea that they'd see the truth - they'd realise this was their grandchild, and they'd relent."

She then recalls a woman from the agency wearing a white coat, a stethoscope and a pearl necklace appearing and taking her daughter.

"This woman carried [my daughter] away, turned around and said 'say bye-bye' and waved her little hand at me," she said, "As if this was the most banal thing."

"And I have never felt so broken in my entire life."

Defries met her daughter again in 1992 when she was 18.

"When you first meet the person you lost, there is grief as well as joy, as well of a sense of expectation," she said.

Later, she became the chair of the Movement for an Adoption Apology, which campaigned for the UK government to apologise for forced adoptions. That was delivered in July by then-Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer.

It came with a promise of £4m to assist in funding a national online resource, led by charity CoramBAAF with the Archives and Records Association, to help people find out where adoption records are held.

Defries believes the apology, and funding, will help.

Through requests to the Sisters of Nazareth, she has tried to get her own records, and received a redacted copy of a register that showed she was at the home.

But she has also requested administrative files and financial records, to get a better understanding of how the home operated.

She said the order told her they had been obliged by law to destroy many of the other records she asked for.

She still believes they may exist, and that privately held records like those could help people understand their experiences, or could hold clues to other potential injustices - not only in homes run by the Sisters of Nazareth, but in similar institutions across the UK.

"What hasn't yet been explored here is all the babies who died in the homes, and were buried in unmarked graves, and the women who suffered birth injuries that weren't repaired, and the women who died," she said.

"And the different things that have gone on that are not being explored because they're yet to be properly recognised," she said. "And the records are hidden, or protected."

The Sisters of Nazareth allow requests for both remote enquiries and on-site research, but visits must be approved by the congregation and are supervised.

There are further restrictions around accessing material containing personal information, that is business-sensitive, or has not yet been appraised, according to the congregation's access policy.

Dr Michael Lambert is a historian at Lancaster University who has investigated mother-and-baby homes.

He supported the campaign for an adoption apology by providing evidence from his own research.

Some of that research was carried out with access to the records granted by the relevant diocese.

Lambert said they indicated many more infant deaths in a Church of England home than had previously been revealed.

He argued it was impossible to know what records were and were not held by a particular congregation or order if they controlled who could see them.

"Allowing an independent person come and look and see is important to be able to gauge that," he said.

"Previous experience tells me that these records could be the key to unlocking peoples'... understanding of the history of the homes."

Often, he said, records had been destroyed because they were deemed to contain other peoples' personal information, or because they were bulky.

But on some occasions, he said, he had been told that records run by homes of different religious orders were "destroyed in floods, fires... only for it later to transpire that they have been preserved".

He said private records like this could help unlock important "linked" records.

For example, he said, correspondence between those who ran mother-and-baby homes and local health authorities could help women learn whether they were given the carcinogenic lactation suppressant Diethylstilbestrol, which was used widely across the NHS until the 1970s, after giving birth.

The Sisters of Nazareth told the BBC that there was no correspondence in its archive, but that research was being carried out on materials held in the National Archives relating to Nazareth Houses, and it believed there were "probably records of this kind held there."

articles.title: Man in court charged with murder over Armadale shooting
articles.summary: Billy Watson was pronounced dead after police were called to a property in the West Lothian town on Saturday morning.
articles.body:
A man has appeared in court charged with murdering another man who was shot dead in West Lothian.

Police were called to a property on Harestanes Road in Armadale at about 11:50 on Saturday.

Billy Watson, 35, was found injured and died at the scene.

Frank McCarthy, 57, appeared at Livingston Sheriff Court on Friday, charged with murder and attempting to defeat the ends of justice. He made no plea and was remanded in custody.

A 29-year-old man and 44-year-old man have also been arrested in connection with the incident.

Police Scotland said inquiries were ongoing.

Detectives previously said they were also investigating whether a nearby car fire in Netherhouses and a fire at a derelict house on Wotherspoon Crescent on Saturday were linked to the incident.

Uniformed officers were seen in the Netherhouses area where the car was set ablaze. A cordon was also put in place on Wotherspoon Crescent.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said nobody was injured in the fires.

articles.title: Fresh sighting of missing Bolton girl Lillia, 13
articles.summary: Lillia went missing from Bolton last week and has not been seen by her family since.
articles.body:
Police have received fresh CCTV of a girl who has been missing from home for a week.

Lillia, 13, from Bolton, was last seen by her family last Friday, but was seen later that evening in Manchester's Picadilly bus station, and at the Trafford Centre the following day.

Officers who have been handing out hundreds of leaflets to try to locate Lillia have now released new footage of her at a McDonald's restaurant in Piccadilly from Sunday at about 20:20 BST.

Greater Manchester Police Ch Spt Int Helen Critchley said: "Officers are making every effort to locate Lillia, and our team have been working through hours of CCTV footage and exploring every avenue to try and find her."

At a press conference on Thursday, Critchley issued an appeal on behalf of Lillia's mother Jessica, saying: "Lillia, if you see this appeal, please know your family love you, miss you and just want to know that you are safe.

"You are not in any trouble, they simply want you to come home."

Lillia was seen boarding a 247 bus from the Trafford Centre on Saturday, heading in the direction of Altrincham, but it was not known where she got off.

Critchley said the McDonalds sighting was the last confirmed sighting of her, adding: "Our investigation currently covers the whole of Greater Manchester with officers across the force being asked to support our enquiries.

"We are also mindful that Lillia could have travelled outside of the Manchester area and are keeping an open mind regarding this possibility."

The force wants to hear from anyone who may have relevant CCTV or doorbell footage, or who has had any contact with Lillia since she was reported missing.

The teenager is described as slim, about 5ft 5in (1.67m) with light brown hair and glasses, and was last seen wearing a black zip-up hooded top, light blue baggy jeans, and a black Nike backpack.

Critchley added: "If you have any information that could help us find Lillia, I would urge you to come forward. Her family just want her home.

Please report any information, no matter how small."

articles.title: Rajnath hails HAL for delivering 'three aviation platforms from one stage'
articles.summary: Defence News: BENGALURU: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday praised aerospace major Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) for “delivering three indigenous aviation .
articles.body: BENGALURU: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Friday praised aerospace major Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd (HAL) for “delivering three indigenous aviation platforms from one stage” as India’s PSU delivered two FOC LCA Mk1 trainers and three HTT-40 trainer aircraft to the Indian Air Force and four Dhruv NG civilian helicopters to Pawan Hans Ltd from its biggest aircraft complex.However, the defence minister flagged concerns about delays in indigenous defence platforms, saying they “lead to cost escalations and increase the risk of technology obsolescence”. He also called for “realistic project timelines to address delays in ongoing technical projects”. He said this at a time HAL is yet to deliver 180 Tejas MK1A aircraft signed with the IAF in two separate contracts (for 83 jets in 2021 and 97 fighters in 2025 worth over Rs 1.1 lakh crore) owing to issues with missile and radar integration with the combat aircraft. These issues are dragging the HAL delivery timelines of MK1A even as the IAF is desperately in need of fighters with its squadrons depleting to just 29 from ideal 42.5.In presence of civil aviation minister K R Naidu and IAF chief ACM A P Singh, Rajnath also urged “young scientists, engineers, designers, test pilots, and technicians to take it as a challenge to create technologies that do not exist today”. He called upon them to develop capabilities that secure a leading position for India in the global aerospace technology landscape over the coming decade.Calling it a “big milestone” for HAL for delivering three platforms in one day, its CMD Ravi K said his test pilots had taken the efforts of testing these indigenous platforms in extreme conditions to make them eligible for certification.With the handing over of two FOC trainer aircraft on Friday, the HAL has completed the delivery of all 40 LCA Mk1 jets signed in two phases (2006 and 2010). The handover of the HTT-40 flight trainer, now officially named ‘Ankur’, marks the beginning of deliveries under the defence ministry’s 70-aircraft contract. HTT-40 trainer has been a long-pending demand of the IAF that needed an indigenous trainer to train its rookie pilots. Dhruv NG helicopters are the civil-certified version of the Advanced Light Helicopters made for the military.The minister described the handing over as a significant milestone in the nation’s progress towards indigenous aerospace capability, technological self-confidence and self-reliance. “We’ve taken steps to not only provide the opportunity to defence PSUs to advance in the defence sector, but also encourage the private industry, ensuring a level playing field,” he said.He stressed the need to advance systematically in the aerospace sector, terming self-reliance in the domain as the need of the hour. “There can be no sudden ‘big bang’ in the development of aerospace systems. It is a vast and gradual process involving a wide range of components. All the products and components involved represent small rungs on a long ladder; we must move forward one step at a time. Naturally, there would be challenges, but we need to view them as milestones on a larger roadmap to achieve progress in a sector as complex and crucial as aerospace,” he said.Rajnath Singh also termed the handing over ceremony as a symbol of the growing synergy between civil aviation and defence aerospace capabilities, emphasising that the development of a robust aerospace industry should not be limited merely to meeting defence requirements. He called for building an ecosystem capable of effectively addressing the needs of both the civil and military aviation sectors. He expressed confidence that the LCA FOC Trainer will play a crucial role in preparing the pilots for this demanding operational environment. “While the Dhruv-NG exemplifies our indigenous civil aerospace prowess, LCA FOC Trainer stands as a symbol of indigenous military aerospace capability and the maturity of its fighter aircraft ecosystem,” he added.On HTT-40, Rajnath stated that India had, for years, relied on imported aircraft to meet its basic training requirements, but HAL is now indigenously manufacturing HTT-40 to cater to the needs of IAF. Highlighting the aircraft’s export potential, he expressed confidence that the HTT-40 would find demand in international markets and fulfil its intended role in strengthening India’s aerospace capabilities.

articles.title: In 1971, Wilt Chamberlain built his custom Bel-Air estate for about $1 million; after a $6.55 million sale, five-year renovation and a near-$19 million asking price, the home sold for about $9.7 million
articles.summary: Real Estate News: The custom-built Bel-Air home originally created for basketball legend Wilt Chamberlain has sold for about $9.7 million (£7.6 million), ending years o.
articles.body: The custom-built Bel-Air home originally created for basketball legend Wilt Chamberlain has sold for about $9.7 million (£7.6 million), ending years of attempts to sell the large property at a much lower price than its original asking price. According to real estate records published by Mansion Global and Architectural Digest, the property changed hands after being listed on and off the market for several years. The final price was about 48 per cent below its highest asking price of $18.99 million in 2017. Located on a private 2.5-acre hilltop at 15216 Antelo Place, the 9,395-square-foot home was sold by real estate investor Dmitri Novikov to cryptocurrency entrepreneur Erik Voorhees. Coldwell Banker Realty managed the sale.Building a home for an NBA giantChamberlain commissioned the house in 1971 while playing for the Los Angeles Lakers. He spent about $1 million to build the unusual property. Architect David Tenneson Rich designed the home, which Chamberlain named "Ursa Major." The name refers to the constellation that includes the Big Dipper and connects to one of Chamberlain's most famous basketball nicknames. The design was strongly influenced by architect Frank Lloyd Wright's ideas about organic architecture. It combined bold, concrete-like shapes with natural materials such as redwood, glass and Bouquet Canyon stone. The house was designed around the 7-foot-1 basketball star's size. It included a 14-foot-high front door weighing more than 2,000 pounds, 40-foot cathedral ceilings in the main living room and custom furniture made to fit Chamberlain. While Chamberlain owned the home, it became well known for its unusual interior features. These included a 15-foot-deep swimming pool that extended directly into the living room, a sunken conversation area and a room with mirrored ceilings and a velvet waterbed. Chamberlain lived at the Bel-Air estate until his death in 1999 at age 63.Years of renovation and changesAfter Chamberlain's death, the property changed owners. In 2008, investor Dmitri Novikov bought it for $6.55 million. Novikov then began a major five-year renovation to modernize the home and increase its overall space. The goal was to combine modern luxury with the home's original mid-century design. According to listing information reported by Mansion Global, the renovation removed some of Chamberlain's most recognizable features, including the mirrored ceiling and the indoor section of the swimming pool.The updated 9,395-square-foot home now includes:Five bedrooms and eight bathrooms.A modern chef's kitchen with high-end appliances and custom cabinets.A private screening room and media lounge.A game room with a pool table and wet bar.A fully equipped gym with a redwood sauna.An updated primary suite with large glass walls and private outdoor terraces overlooking the Stone Canyon Reservoir and the ocean.Despite the changes, the house kept its original 40-foot living room ceiling, large stone fireplace and heavy timber support beams.Price cuts in the Los Angeles luxury marketThe home was first listed after the renovation in 2017 for $18.99 million. After failing to find a buyer, it was removed from the market and listed again several times over the next seven years. The price fell to $14.9 million in 2020 and then to $11.99 million in 2022. The property eventually sold for $9.675 million. Although that was far below the original $18.99 million asking price, the sale still gave Novikov a profit compared with the $6.55 million he paid in 2008. The sale comes as conditions in Los Angeles' luxury housing market continue to change. High-end homes have faced longer selling periods and greater pressure on prices following the introduction of the city's Measure ULA transfer tax on expensive real estate sales.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: iPhone 18, AirPods 5 and Apple Watch Series 12 are out today — here’s what to know before you shop
articles.summary: Apple released its iPhone 18, Apple Watch Series 12 and AirPods 5. Here’s everything you need to know about the new products.
articles.body: Apple’s iPhone 18, AirPods 5 and Apple Watch Series 12 officially hit shelves today, and if you’re trying to decide whether it’s time to upgrade — or which items actually make sense for you — I’ve got you covered. I’m breaking down everything you need to know about this newest lineup, from what’s actually different to pricing and availability. Apple’s latest launches The AirPods 5 deliver up to 1.5 times more active noise cancellation than the previous generation and are powered by a new H2 chip. They also have dynamic head tracking, adaptive audio to switch between noise cancelling and transparency mode, depending on your environment. Similar to other AirPod models, they also have IP57 rating for dust, sweat, and water resistance. On the software side, they offer hands-free access to the new Siri AI and real-time Live Translation. Battery life is up to four hours with ANC with the base model, or five hours (22 total with the case) with the USB-C Wireless Charging Case option, which also supports Qi and Apple Watch charging. NBC Selected senior editor Shalwah Evans tried out the AirPods 5 after receiving a pair from the brand and immediately noticed that the open earbuds fit more comfortably than previous models. “I was pleasantly surprised that these pods with no rubber tip didn’t budge,” she says. “I also love how crisp the ambient sound is when ANC is turned off, which is a huge plus for when I’m walking my dog and need to be aware of my surroundings crossing busy streets.” The new AirPods 5 start at $129 and are available now. The new iPhone 18 Pro holds onto its familiar silhouette, but the real story is underneath. Both the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max (also available today) now run on Apple’s new A20 Pro chip paired with a redesigned vapor chamber that Apple says delivers up to 40 percent better sustained performance than last year’s model. The camera system gets a meaningful bump too, with a 48-megapixel main camera that now features variable aperture, letting the lens physically adjust for sharper low-light shots and more control over depth. This marks the first time that technology has appeared on an iPhone. The biggest difference between the two models is screen size — 6.3 inches on the Pro versus 6.9 inches on the Max — and battery life, which Apple is calling the largest leap in iPhone history. Under Apple’s “typical use” metric, the Pro is rated for up to 24 hours per charge, while the Max stretches to 30 hours. Both phones also charge faster than before, reaching 50 percent in about 15 minutes with a compatible adapter. In terms of pricing, the iPhone 18 Pro starts at $1,199, a $100 increase from the previous model, while the Pro Max starts at $1,299. Both phones are available for purchase now. The Apple Watch Series 12 centers on a completely reworked Health Sensing System, powered by the new S11 chip. Larger, more power-efficient green LEDs let the optical and electrical sensors work harder in the background — taking heart rate readings every five seconds and measuring heart rate variability up to 24 times more often than the Series 11, according to Apple. That stream of data feeds directly into a new Readiness score: a single number, calculated each morning from your recent activity, vitals and sleep, meant to tell you at a glance how much you can take on that day. The design has gotten an upgrade too. It’s available in eight finishes, including two ceramic options in Pearl White and Night Blue, and the aluminum models now use Ceramic Shield 2, which Apple says is 60 percent tougher than the previous Ion-X glass. Beyond health tracking, Series 12 leans into AI with new Siri-powered features, including Live Rewind, which lets you replay the last 15 seconds of audio you just missed, and Siri Recap, which generates quick summaries of conversations picked up by the watch’s microphone (a feature you program and can customize). It keeps the familiar 42mm and 46mm case sizes, along with standard safety staples like Fall Detection and Emergency SOS, and is rated WR50 and IP6X for water and dust resistance. It starts at $399 — the same price as the Series 11 — and is available now. The Apple Watch Ultra 4 is built around the same S11 chip and redesigned Health Sensing System as the Series 12, but tuned for endurance athletes and outdoor use. Battery life gets a major boost too: Apple rates it for up to 50 hours of everyday use, up to 18 hours of standard workout tracking with full GPS and heart rate monitoring, and up to 45 hours in a new Max Extended Workout mode — enough to cover a 100-mile race. It’s available in two titanium finishes, natural and black, and retains the built-in satellite communications that let wearers stay connected off the grid. Like the Series 12, the Ultra 4 also has Siri AI and Audio Intelligence features powered by the S11 chip, plus the ability to start a request on iPhone and pick it up seamlessly on the watch. It keeps the rugged design and precision dual-frequency GPS that have defined the Ultra line. Pricing holds steady at $799, the same as the Ultra 3, and it can be purchased now. Want more from NBC Select? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. Why trust NBC Selected? I am a commerce editor at NBC Selected and a journalist who regularly covers wellness, lifestyle and more. I have written about the “no-touch” phone law, the best screen protectors and more. For this story, I researched all of Apple’s new offerings and watched their announcement event. articles.title: Yemen war escalates: 1.12 lakh displaced, thousands flee to Djibouti
articles.summary: Middle East News: The escalating conflict in Yemen has displaced at least 1.12 lakh people inside the country in the past two weeks, while thousands have fled across th.
articles.body: The escalating conflict in Yemen has displaced at least 1.12 lakh people inside the country in the past two weeks, while thousands have fled across the Gulf of Aden to Djibouti, according to the United Nations.Nearly 3,000 people have reached Djibouti in less than a week, as renewed fighting between Iran-aligned Houthi forces and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces pushes more families to flee, Sandrine Desamours, the UN refugee agency's representative in Djibouti, told Reuters.Djibouti's government is preparing for the arrival of as many as 10,000 refugees, Desamours said, warning that such an influx could place acute pressure on the country's healthcare and education systems.According to the UN International Organisation for Migration (IOM), many people are making the perilous journey aboard overcrowded boats, arriving with little food or water. Most are Yemeni families seeking refuge in Djibouti, although the IOM has also recorded a smaller number of migrants, mainly from Ethiopia, travelling towards the country.The UN refugee agency has also reported increased arrivals from Yemen in Somaliland and Puntland. Those arrivals include Yemeni refugees as well as Somali refugees returning to the region, although their numbers remain in the hundreds.Houthi offensive expandsThe latest escalation comes as the Iran-aligned Houthis have intensified attacks on southern Saudi Arabia and its energy infrastructure, while expanding their territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast towards the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, one of the world's key maritime chokepoints. Saudi Arabia and forces backing Yemen's internationally recognised government have responded with airstrikes on Houthi positions.The Houthis have made significant gains along the Red Sea coast, including the capture of the strategic port city of Mokha and advances towards the Bab el-Mandeb. The group also reached the strategic Perim Island in the strait earlier this month.The renewed fighting is adding another layer to Yemen's already devastating humanitarian crisis. The country has been ravaged by years of civil war between the Houthis and forces backing the internationally recognised government, leaving its economy, healthcare system and basic infrastructure severely weakened.The battle for Yemen's western coast also carries significance beyond the country. The Bab el-Mandeb Strait connects the Red Sea with the Gulf of Aden and is a critical route for global shipping and energy supplies. Greater Houthi control of the area could give Iran-aligned forces additional leverage over a vital maritime corridor, particularly amid the wider US-Iran conflict and disruption around the Strait of Hormuz.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Sweden’s left-wing opposition leader begins efforts to form government
articles.summary: Magdalena Andersson will likely face several challenges as she tries to get Sweden’s other left-wing parties to unite.
articles.body:
Sweden’s opposition leader has officially begun talks to form a coalition government after the country’s left-wing bloc won a slim majority in last week’s election .

Magdalena Andersson, leader of the centre-left Social Democrats, was asked by Parliament Speaker Andreas Norlen on Friday to begin efforts to form a new government.

Norlen’s request follows the resignation of centre-right Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson, who stepped down on Thursday after the general election result was confirmed.

“I have now been tasked with exploring the possibility of forming a government. A task I undertake with great humility and will act constructively to put together a new government,” Andersson said in a statement posted on Instagram.

“My approach to the work that is now taking place is that all political forces now need to put party tactics aside and put Sweden and the Swedish people first.”

Andersson will likely face a series of challenges as she tries to persuade Sweden’s other left-wing parties to unite and form a new administration. The left-wing bloc won 176 of Parliament’s 349 seats in last week’s vote, securing a razor-thin majority of three seats.

Andersson is expected to seek the support of three other left-wing parties: the Greens, the Centre Party and the Left Party.

The socialist Left Party says Andersson will have to award some of its MPs cabinet posts to win their support. However, the liberal Centre Party insists it will not support such a government.

Andersson has until September 28 to form a government. If she fails, Kristersson, whose centre-right bloc won 173 seats, will try to form a coalition.

Coalition and minority governments are common in Sweden because the country has two major left- and right-wing blocs, both of which contain four parties.

The process of forming a government following the 2022 election took more than a month.

articles.title: Trump admin sued over possible ICE deployment at US midterm polling sites
articles.summary: US News: A coalition of civil rights groups has sued the Trump administration, seeking to prevent US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents and other.
articles.body: A coalition of civil rights groups has sued the Trump administration, seeking to prevent US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents and other federal law-enforcement officers from being deployed at polling sites during the November midterm elections.The lawsuit, led by the NAACP, was filed Friday in a US federal court and argues that the administration's stated possibility of deploying federal officers at polling locations could amount to voter intimidation, The Guardian reported.The groups have also challenged increased federal scrutiny of voter rolls.According to the complaint, such actions could discourage people from voting, particularly Black, Latino and Asian voters, naturalised citizens and members of mixed-status families.The groups cited comments by senior Trump administration officials about the possible presence of federal agents at polling locations. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said earlier this month that ICE would not patrol polling sites but could be present if there was a threat at a location or if agents were serving a warrant.The administration has previously said that ICE does not plan operations targeting polling locations. DHS has maintained that the agency conducts targeted enforcement and could respond if an active public-safety threat emerged at a polling site.However, President Donald Trump has previously declined to rule out sending ICE officers or National Guard personnel to polling locations during the midterms, contributing to concerns among voting-rights groups.What the lawsuit saysThe groups argue that deploying armed federal personnel at election sites would violate federal law and that the threat of such a presence could intimidate voters. They also cited provisions of the Voting Rights Act that prohibit intimidation, threats or coercion against people exercising their right to vote.The lawsuit is at least the second legal challenge this month seeking to prevent federal immigration agents from being present at polling locations during the midterms.The Guardian reported that the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security had been asked for comment on the lawsuit. The FBI declined to comment, while ICE referred questions to DHS.Federal law separately prohibits armed federal officers or members of the armed forces from being stationed at locations where elections are being held, subject to a narrow exception involving armed enemies of the US.So far, the Trump administration has not deployed armed federal officers or military personnel at polling locations for the upcoming midterm elections. articles.title: JP Morgan struggling to forecast oil prices due to US-Iran war
articles.summary: The bank said it "assumed" there would be economic red lines, like oil at $100 a barrel, that the US would be unwilling the cross.
articles.body:
Investment banking giant JP Morgan has said it is struggling to predict how oil prices will be impacted by the US-Iran war, telling investors in a rare note that "we simply don't know how to model the endgame".

The bank said it assumed at the start of the conflict that there would be "economic red lines" that the Trump administration would be unwilling to cross, and therefore it believed a deal would have been struck to open up the Strait of Hormuz shipping lane back in June.

It said such red lines included oil prices rising above $100 a barrel, inflation reaching 4%, gasoline topping $5 a gallon and rates on 10-year government borrowing hitting 5%.

JP Morgan is a huge name in the financial world, so for the investment bank to admit its experts are grappling with working out the economic impact of the US-Iran conflict reflects the tricky nature of trying to predict President Donald Trump's next moves.

An oil and gas industry source told the BBC it was "unusual" for such a high-profile investment firm to issue such a note, but added it was a "reflection on the state of play", given the uncertainties around the conflict.

Investors often make investment decisions on inflation expectations and the price of oil is a major factor in prices rising across the world, given the commodity's widespread use and humanity's dependence on it.

While gasoline remains below $5 and inflation has also not reached 4%, oil prices have surged back above $100 in recent weeks and the interest rate - known as a yield - on government bonds, which are issued in order for the US to borrow money from financial markets, has ticked over 5%.

"Six months later [since the war began], many of those lines have been crossed, yet the exit strategy is less clear, not more," said the commodities research team at JP Morgan in note.

"For the first time since the start of the Iran conflict, we don't have a baseline view. We simply don't know how to model the endgame."
