US borrowing costs hit fresh highs over inflation fears

US President Donald Trump said last week he did not think the Iran war would end until after November's midterm elections in the US.

"Right after the election, oil prices are going to be tumbling downward," Trump told reporters last week. "I think it's going to take a little bit longer than the midterm."

High oil prices have been behind the rising cost of living in the US and around the world, with fuel and energy prices surging ahead of the colder months.

The US central bank, the Federal Reserve, raised interest rates this week for the first time in more than three years and signaled they could be increased further this year and into 2027 in an effort to slow rising prices.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh said the move was because "inflation is too high and has been for too long", though Trump disagreed with the decision.

In JP Morgan's note, analysts said it estimated the "fair value" for oil in September would be around $90 a barrel, despite it trading above $100.

But it said "the market is pricing in the risk" of more disruption to trade.

Analysts cited further risks to oil supply in the Middle East, with Yemen's Houthis, which are backed by Iran, seizing an area at the mouth of the waterway in the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is another key international shipping route.

The conflict between Russia and Ukraine also continues to have an impact.

Analysts said with "no clear signals" of the war de-escalating, the assumption that global oil supply disruption was temporary is "becoming increasingly difficult to sustain".

articles.title: A professor took his niece metal detecting in a Suffolk field and found 18 Iron Age gold coins
articles.summary: UK News: A University of East Anglia professor who took his niece metal detecting in a Suffolk field uncovered a hoard of 18 Iron Age gold coins linked to 2 an.
articles.body: A University of East Anglia professor who took his niece metal detecting in a Suffolk field uncovered a hoard of 18 Iron Age gold coins linked to 2 ancient British rulers. Tom Licence, Professor of Medieval History and Literature at UEA, discovered the coins during searches in a field near Bury St Edmunds, Suffolk, in autumn 2024, before returning months later and finding another full coin. The discoveries were reported to a Finds Liaison Officer and declared treasure. The resulting Bury St Edmunds hoard has been described by auction house Noonans as the largest known hoard of gold coins deposited during the reign of Dubnovellaunos, ruler of the Trinovantes. Sixteen of the 18 coins were subsequently offered individually at Noonans Mayfair on March 4, 2026, after Licence and the landowner each retained one stater. Those 16 auctioned coins fetched a combined hammer price of £33,200, exceeding Noonans' pre-sale estimate of around £25,000.A field chosen for his niece produced the first gold staterLicence had been interested in metal detecting since childhood and developed a more serious interest in the hobby in 1994, after finding a Charles I Rose Farthing in a flower bed in Rye, East Sussex. According to Noonans, he chose the Suffolk field because his niece wanted to try metal detecting and he was looking for a suitable place to take her. The field rose gently from a nearby stream and had dark, silty soil that was in good condition when Licence searched it. The first signals produced 2 pieces of Viking hack silver. Licence then found a gold stater. After changing his detector settings and systematically working along marked rows, he uncovered several more gold coins before finishing for the day. He subsequently returned to the field and continued searching, ultimately finding the coins that became the Bury St Edmunds hoard. The finds were reported through the Portable Antiquities Scheme and declared treasure under the Treasure Act. Licence was born in Essex but said his family has roots around Bury St Edmunds. Following the discovery, he said he liked to imagine that the coins could have been buried by one of his own ancestors.The coins carry the names of 2 Iron Age rulersThe coins in the hoard can be attributed to Addedomaros and Dubnovellaunos, 2 rulers whose coinages are associated with the Catuvellauni and Trinovantes. Noonans' catalogue notes that Addedomaros' territory appears to have extended into Trinovantian land and that he may have been the father of Dubnovellaunos, although the relationship is not established as fact. Addedomaros was probably the first king north of the River Thames to produce an inscribed coinage. His coins carry his name in Latin letters, providing rare evidence of written names on British coinage before the Roman conquest.Dubnovellaunos ruled the Trinovantes and at one stage also appears to have held power in Kent. His name is also recorded outside Britain. The Res Gestae Divi Augusti, the account of Roman Emperor Augustus' achievements, mentions a ruler named Dubnovellaunus among foreign kings who sought refuge with Augustus. Numismatist John Sills has suggested that the hoard was buried during Dubnovellaunos' reign. His interpretation is based partly on the sequence of coin dies and the absence of Dubnovellaunos' final 2 issues from the group. The chronology of the rulers and their coinages remains subject to scholarly discussion.The burial site matches a pattern seen in other hoardsThe findspot lies roughly a day's walk from Colchester to the south and Bury St Edmunds to the north, placing it within the area associated with the Trinovantes. The physical position of the coins also attracted attention because the hoard was found just below the crest of an east-facing slope. Noonans cites researcher Philip de Jersey's work on the microtopography of Iron Age and later coin hoards, which identified a preference for burial on east-facing slopes among hoards deposited on hillsides. The Bury St Edmunds discovery fits that pattern.Licence has suggested that the combination of a hillcrest illuminated by the morning sun and a nearby spring could indicate that the location held some form of religious significance for the people who buried the coins. That remains an interpretation rather than an established explanation for the burial. The concentration of the coins in one location indicates a deliberate deposit, but there is no definitive evidence explaining why they were buried or why they were never recovered. Their survival for roughly 2,000 years before Licence's detector located them has provided numismatists with a rare group of inscribed British gold coins from the period immediately before Roman rule.Two standout coins reveal more about Iron Age coinageAmong the hoard's highlights was an Addedomaros wheel stater that Licence identified as a personal favourite. Numismatist John Sills noted that the coin carries more visible lettering than any other known example of the type, helping confirm the spelling of the ruler's name on the design. Before the auction, Noonans estimated the coin at £3,000 to £6,000. Another notable piece was a Dubnovellaunos stater struck from a previously unrecorded die, which had a pre-sale estimate of £1,500 to £2,000. The coins were offered individually rather than as a single lot, allowing collectors to acquire individual examples of the 2 rulers' coinages.Sixteen of the 18 coins from the discovery went under the hammer at Noonans in March 2026, after Licence and the landowner each retained one stater for themselves. The sale of those 16 lots produced a combined hammer price of £33,200, above the auction house's original estimate of around £25,000. Licence has said he plans to put some of his share of the proceeds towards supporting archaeological work in Suffolk, giving the discovery a connection to the region where the coins spent centuries buried beneath the field.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: The Gentlemen 'could bring tourism boost to West'
articles.summary: Locations in Gloucestershire and Wiltshire were used in Guy Ritchie's latest blockbuster series.
articles.body:
Some of the West's most prominent locations have been used as the backdrop for Guy Ritchie's The Gentlemen.

Some of the scenes for the Netflix show were filmed in parts of Gloucestershire and Wiltshire, including Badminton House and Salisbury Cathedral.

It is not the first time that the region has been used as a setting for big budget productions and it is hoped that the exposure could lead to something of a tourism boom in the area.

"[Shows like The Gentlemen are] a really good way to introduce people to places they might not have known about," said Lucy Dodsworth, a travel writer and founder of the Explore the Cotswolds website.

"Obviously, Salisbury Cathedral is very famous, but villages like Castle Combe or Tetbury from Rivals gets people to see them on screen and want to come and see them in real life," she said.

Dodsworth said the beauty of the Cotswolds makes a great backdrop as the area looks like "how you would imagine England to".

"You can use it for lots of different time periods because a lot of things haven't changed for a long period, and there's so many beautiful stately homes to choose from," she added.

Gloucestershire's Badminton House plays a prominent role in the gangster-comedy blockbuster as the ancestral home of main protagonist, Eddie Horniman.

Other big money productions recently filmed in the area include Star Wars and Bridgerton.

Fans line street for EMF star's final farewell

No more 'missing link' as new route opens

'I am a survivor but I am also so many other things'

Filming can also provide an additional source of revenue for sites, helping to fund their ongoing upkeep and maintenance.

"It costs us nearly £20,000 a day to open the doors and keep it looking tip-top," said Tim Croall, from Salisbury Cathedral, which was used as the setting for a grand coronation scene.

"That's a lot of money, so we rely on the generosity of visitors, donors and income streams such as location filming."

The filming also brings some well known faces to the local area, giving locals a chance to rub shoulders with the stars.

"Guy Ritchie was very interested in the cathedral," said Croall, "I think it might have been his idea to base it here."

"He was very interested in parts of the cathedral, the oldest parts, some of our oldest windows, looking at Magna Carta itself."

Croall also met actor Theo James, who plays the protagonist, Eddie Horniman.

"He was great, very nice, very unassuming, kept himself to himself when he wasn't being asked to film and then did his filming, a professional actor," he said.

articles.title: Early in-person voting begins in the 2026 US midterm elections in Virginia
articles.summary: Virginia leads the way for in-person voting, reflecting a nationwide trend towards casting ballots before Election Day.
articles.body:
Virginia has kicked off in-person voting for the 2026 United States midterm elections, as voters there become among the first in the country to cast ballots in this year’s congressional and state elections.

The start of early voting on Friday – critical in deciding who controls the House and the Senate for the remainder of US President Donald Trump’s term – reflects a 25-year expansion effort by states to cast ballots before Election Day on November 3.

“Why not just have a little fun in life, you know, try to be the first early voter?” said college student Sanya Singhal, who was among the first to vote early in person in Virginia. “I really want to participate in my democracy.”

The number of states offering options to vote before November expanded from 24 in 2000 to 47 in 2026, plus Washington, in the District of Columbia. But early-voting periods, eligibility requirements, and procedures vary widely by state.

Virginia , where early voting began Friday, expanded weekend early voting and dropped its absentee witness requirement. Mail-in ballots postmarked by Election Day can now arrive by noon three days after Election Day.

Voters in a few other states, including Minnesota and South Dakota, can cast absentee ballots in person, typically at a local election office or voting centre. And North Carolina began mailing absentee ballots on September 4 to voters who requested them. More expansive early voting is scheduled to begin in those and other states in the coming weeks.

Mail-in voting is particularly significant this year, as the Trump administration has brought multiple legal challenges seeking to restrict its use. In June , the Supreme Court ruled that federal law does not override state laws allowing certain postmarked absentee ballots to arrive after Election Day, leaving existing state deadlines in place.

A Supreme Court ruling this week blocked President Donald Trump’s attempt to impose new federal restrictions on mail voting, leaving state laws in place for the midterms. The proposed changes included standardised ballot envelopes and a federal system for verifying voter eligibility.

The Postal Service has nevertheless advised voters who use mail ballots to send them earlier rather than later.

articles.title: Driver who killed woman in Leicester celebrating 60th birthday jailed
articles.summary: Donna Brighton was thrown into the road through the open window of a taxi, a court hears.
articles.body:
A speeding driver has been jailed for two years after he caused the death of a passenger in a taxi when he crashed into the vehicle in Leicester.

Thomas Goulty killed grandmother Donna Brighton when she was thrown from the taxi through an open window in Glenfield Road on 16 September 2023.

Brother and sister Steve and Andrea Sidsaff, who were also passengers in the back of the taxi, were seriously injured in the collision, Leicester Crown Court heard.

On Friday, Goulty, 36, of Aikman Avenue, Leicester, was sentenced after admitting causing Brighton's death and causing serious injuries to the other passengers by careless driving.

The court heard Goulty drank two lagers before he drove his silver Vauxhall Astra at 64mph in a residential 30mph limit area before crashing into 69-year-old Sarwar Mohammad's Peugeot Expert Tepee taxi.

Mohammad, of Willow Brook Road in Leicester, who had been driving the taxi and admitted the same offences, was handed a six-month prison sentence, suspended for two years, and told he must do 100 hours of unpaid work.

Prosecutor Steven Bailey told the court Brighton did not know the Sidsaffs, who had come to Leicester for the Radio 2 in the Park music festival, but they shared a taxi because they were going in the same direction.

Brighton, who was from the city, had been out with her friends celebrating her 60th birthday.

Bailey said the collision happened as a result of the "combined bad driving of Thomas Goulty and Sarwar Mohammad", while the taxi was making a right turn towards Westfield Road across the central reservation of the dual carriageway.

Goulty had been out in the city and sent someone a message minutes before the crash saying he was "just out having a couple of beers", and in a roadside test immediately after the crash tested positive for alcohol in his breath, but later assessments could not conclude that he was over the driving limit.

Bailey said Goulty's speed was "excessive", up to 64mph (102km/h) on approach and 55mph at the point of impact.

"He had left himself little or no calculation time and any braking was far too late," he said.

"He drove too quickly for the road and its conditions, about twice the speed limit, having taken alcohol and in the dark."

Bailey told the court it seemed Brighton was helping Mohammad with directions as to where to turn and when to turn when he "allowed himself to become distracted".

The court heard he was driving lawfully at 25mph in the 30mph zone before he slowed to 8mph to carry out the right-hand turn, but Bailey said "crucially he did not come to a stop fully" and "did not maximise his chances of avoiding the collision".

Brighton "was thrown out of the taxi through the open window into the road", Bailey said, and suffered fatal head and chest injuries, while the other two passengers suffered serious injuries, including several fractured bones.

Barristers for both defendants told the court they are remorseful about what happened.

Sentencing the defendants, Recorder Jacob Hallam KC said: "You took Donna Brighton's life, and the people who loved her are still paying the price of that today, and you caused the Sidsaffs, as I have said, terrible injuries."

Goulty has been disqualified from driving for five years and must take an extended retest, while Mohammad was disqualified for two years but will not need to take an extended retest.

articles.title: Pentagon resumes mandatory testosterone testing for US troops over 30
articles.summary: Experts have called policy unnecessary and said testosterone injections could increase risks of infertility.
articles.body:
The United States military says it is moving forward with a policy of mandatory testosterone testing among US service members aged 30 and older, following an earlier pause and questions from medical experts.

The Pentagon released new guidelines for the policy, championed by Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth , on Friday.

Hegseth first announced the policy in July, stating that it was needed to identify potential “testosterone deficiency” and enable soldiers to operate at their “absolute best”.

The move aligns with interest from online podcasters and health influencers who have touted testosterone injections as a means of becoming healthier and more muscular.

A Pentagon release quotes Hegseth as saying the measure is about “restoring and optimising your natural capabilities, protecting your longevity and ensuring you have the biological foundation required to sustain the fight”.

Medical experts have described the programme as unnecessary and said that it could cause potential health complications such as infertility for service members, if applied incorrectly. The Pentagon temporarily paused an earlier version of the policy in September in order to “allow for updates”.

The new guidelines apply only to male service members and establish uniform screening standards and treatment pathways for testosterone deficiencies. Testing will take place during periodic health assessments and annual evaluations, and younger service members can request testing if they want.

Hegseth has promoted a heavy focus on policies that he says are necessary to maximise military preparedness but that critics say are importing right-wing culture war issues into the military.

The Trump administration has banned transgender service members, rolled back protections meant to minimise civilian harm in military operations, and ousted military officials seen as at odds with the government’s priorities.

“While we invest heavily in our weapon systems, platforms and gear, our most decisive tactical advantage will always be the individual warfighter,” Hegseth said.

articles.title: Trump administration starts building border wall in Texas’ Big Bend region
articles.summary: It marks the first major construction in an area of the U.S.-Mexico border where the administration’s plans have met with heavy opposition.
articles.body: COMSTOCK, Texas — The Trump administration has started building the border wall through a west Texas section of the Big Bend region, marking the first major construction in an area of the U.S.-Mexico border where the administration’s plans have met with heavy opposition. The start of construction marks an important milestone in the administration’s $46 billion plan to line the border with walls, barriers, roads and technology as it seeks to make good on a key campaign promise by President Donald Trump to finish the wall. And it comes as Customs and Border Protection says it has doubled the pace at which it is building the wall across the U.S.-Mexico border. Customs and Border Protection said in a statement to The Associated Press that “border wall panel installation is underway” in a 47-mile stretch of Hudspeth County in west Texas known as Big Bend 1. There are a total of five project areas that make up the roughly 500-mile Big Bend region stretching from an area of Hudspeth County south of El Paso to Lake Amistad. The agency did not say when the panels had been installed. On a map on the agency’s website where it posts updates of wall construction across the entire southern border, a photo showed a crane lifting one of the 30-foot tall steel wall panels into place while construction workers looked on. The new activity was separate from a border infrastructure project in the nearby Big Bend National Park, where the administration has temporarily suspended construction in an attempt at outreach to opponents. In the broader Big Bend region of Texas, CBP has run up against concerted opposition from landowners, environmental groups, business owners and ranchers who say the remote region isn’t a high traffic area for illegal immigration. Activists said Friday they would continue opposing the border infrastructure projects in the rest of the Big Bend region, even as the panels were being installed. Clara Benson, one of the founders of the No Big Bend Wall Coalition which has been fighting against CBP’s plans, said in an interview Friday that the organization had been receiving reports of trucks moving supplies into the remote area along the Rio Grande and that contractors had been clearing yards to stage supplies. But speaking from Washington, D.C. where she and others in the coalition were meeting with lawmakers, she said that the organization and others would continue to fight the wall-building plans across the region. “We will continue to fight for this land no matter what the outcome is. We will continue fighting to the end,” said Benson. “You talk to people in west Texas and they say even if they put it up, we’ll fight for them to take it down. So this fight is not over.” The news comes as the administration is speeding forward with a plan to line the entire border with a combination of 30-foot tall steel bollard walls, barriers designed to stop vehicles from crossing the border, new patrol roads and various technologies to deter and detect migrants or smugglers from crossing the border. Customs and Border Protection said that they are building an average of 12 miles of barriers a week across the 2,000-mile border with Mexico and recently hit a milestone of 200 miles of new barriers built since the second Trump administration took office. The 12-miles a week average is double the pace that the agency’s head, Rodney Scott, cited earlier this year. The agency has faced opposition from environmental groups, a small town that worries the wall will cause flooding in its area, Native Americans who say the construction is disturbing sacred sites and landowners who say the construction will infringe on their land. In Texas much of the opposition has centered on the agency’s plans for Big Bend National Park, in the state’s southwest on the Rio Grande that is a draw for tourists from around the world. But up and down river outside the park, much of the land is owned by private landowners, many of whom have pushed back against the government’s efforts. Earlier this week, landowners, ranchers and business owners in the Big Bend region along with a nonprofit organization dedicated to protecting the region’s landscape and heritage sued to stop the administration’s plans. Activists and landowners have also shown up at county meetings to push their elected officials not to cooperate with contractors hired by CBP to build the wall, and many landowners have refused to allow government officials or contractors onto their land to survey it.

articles.title: Two injured by Israeli shelling as troops advance in southern Lebanon
articles.summary: Israeli forces withdraw from outskirts of a town in southern Lebanon after a standoff with Lebanese forces.
articles.body:
Israeli artillery shelling has injured two people in southern Lebanon as Israeli troops separately advanced towards border towns and clashed with Lebanese soldiers.

The two people were injured in shelling on Chaqra in the Bint Jbeil district of Nabatieh governorate and were taken to Tebnin hospital, Lebanon’s state-run National News Agency reported on Friday.

Israeli artillery shells also fell in Wadi Nahla on the outskirts of Shuqra, the agency added, and Israeli forces withdrew from the outskirts of Deir Mimas in Marjayoun after advancing earlier in the day towards the entrance to the town.

Israel has been occupying a swath of southern Lebanon since war broke out in March between Israel and the Lebanese group Hezbollah. The Lebanese army is supposed to gradually take control of the area under a June framework agreement between the two countries.

The standoff around Deir Mimas began when two Israeli tanks advanced along a road towards the town and stopped in front of a dirt barricade with Lebanese army vehicles stationed on the other side.

The Lebanese military said its army patrol had established a temporary observation post on the outskirts of Deir Mimas on September 10 in coordination with the military coordination group for Lebanon, the US-backed trilateral body that manages deconfliction between Israel and Lebanon.

“An Israeli occupation force approached the newly established post located within the so-called security zone and threw sound bombs in the vicinity,” the army said in a statement. “In response, the [Lebanese] army reinforced the post, and a state of alert ensued between the two sides.”

National News Agency reported that Israeli forces then withdrew, retreating to their position in neighbouring Tell en-Nhas. Meanwhile, Lebanese troops returned to their main base in the town after contacting the deconfliction group, the Lebanese army said.

Separately on Friday, the Israeli military advanced from the municipality of al-Tiri towards the outskirts of Hadatha in southern Lebanon’s Bint Jbeil district, according to the agency.

In other parts of southern Lebanon, Israeli forces struck the municipalities of al-Mansouri and Majdal Zoun with artillery shelling.

Israeli forces also set fire to the public hospital in the town of Meiss el-Jabal, according to Lebanese state media. Details on the extent of the damage or casualties were not immediately reported.

A US-brokered framework agreement between Lebanon and Israel in June provides for a gradual Israeli withdrawal from Lebanese territory and the deployment of the Lebanese army in areas vacated by Israeli forces.

Despite the agreement, however, Israel has continued attacks on southern Lebanon and occupies areas in the region.

Israeli attacks have killed at least 4,386 people and wounded 12,407 others since March 2, when the current Hezbollah-Israel war erupted.

Lebanon’s Health Ministry said the overall casualties from Israeli attacks since it began its war on Gaza in October 2023 had reached 8,953 killed and 30,643 injured.

articles.title: Macron orders protections for infrastructure, citing a growing Russian threat
articles.summary: PARIS — French President Emmanuel Macron said Friday he had asked his government to prepare a plan to protect critical infrastructure, including sensitive defense industry sites, against drone attacks and cyberattacks amid what he described as an intensifying Russian hybrid threat.
articles.body: PARIS — French President Emmanuel Macron said Friday he had asked his government to prepare a plan to protect critical infrastructure, including sensitive defense industry sites, against drone attacks and cyberattacks amid what he described as an intensifying Russian hybrid threat. “In recent weeks, the threat — particularly the Russian hybrid threat — facing Europeans and France has intensified,” Macron told reporters at the Elysee Palace after meeting political party leaders. Macron specifically cited drone attacks and cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. The European Union describes Russian hybrid activities as including sabotage, cyberattacks, disinformation and interference in democratic processes. Macron warned that the attacks would not go unanswered and accused Moscow of trying to intimidate Europeans into weakening their support for Ukraine. “We are not intimidated,” he said, arguing that Europe’s present and future security was at stake in Ukraine. Macron also said he would convene a Group of Seven meeting in the coming weeks to coordinate the response to the energy crisis. He linked surging energy prices to the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine and disruption to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Macron acknowledged the strain of rising energy costs on households, saying, “The situation is very difficult and distressing for many families.”

articles.title: Indian-origin US diplomat Mahvash Siddiqui says she alerted senior managers about 'Cognizant-like' visa abuse 20 years ago
articles.summary: US News: The US Department of Labor recently announced the suspension of Cognizant from filing new Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) applications as a probe.
articles.body: The US Department of Labor recently announced the suspension of Cognizant from filing new Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) applications as a probe into alleged visa fraud is going on. Mahvash Siddiqui, an Indian-origin US diplomat who worked at the Chennai consulate two decades ago, claimed that junior officers repeatedly told their seniors how IT conglomerates game the visa system but they were never paid any attention.Siddiqui reacted to the PERM cancelation of Cognizant as she wrote an article for Center for Immigration Studies detailing her experience and understanding from the work she had done at the visa frontline 20 years ago. She said even 20 years ago, the workload was immense as they were adjudicating hundreds of visa applications daily. Siddiqui recalled that there was a Business Express program at that time which offered a fast visa adjudication for IT outsourcing firms like TCS, Wipro, Satyam, Infosys, Accenture and Cognizant. But not only foreign IT firms, Us firms like General Electric, Microsoft, and Honeywell, too were also accorded fast services where their employees were granted "top-brass" handling with minimal documentary scrutiny.Corporate facade collapsed at visa interview deskSiddiqui said she had an academic and technical background and two of her sisters were computer engineers. She had sufficient knowledge of computer science and software architecture to question candidates going beyond the expected questions."When basic computer science and engineering concepts were tested during expedited interviews, the corporate facade collapsed quickly across both foreign and domestic multinational applicants," she said, identifying three issues that she encountered during those interviews.Fake degree: Siddiqui said many applicants had no formal degree in computer science but they just completed some brief training modules like short Microsoft Certified Systems Engineer courses or elementary graphic design classes.B1/B2 abuse: Tourist or business visa applicants cited reasons like "gaining knowledge", "project coordination" but they all were placed on-site and then transitioned to H-1B.Third-party corruption: "Third-party recruiters and corrupt corporate HR handlers systematically monetized access to the Business Express Program, charging underqualified individuals illicit fees to slip them into the corporate applicant pool," Siddiqui said."A consular adjudicator sitting at the visa window conducts tens of thousands of interviews per year. Through daily, direct interaction, an officer’s judgment becomes exceptionally refined. Adjudicators learn to detect fraud patterns, recognize rehearsed lines, and identify broader structural patterns across thousands of cases. In contrast, Non-Immigrant Visa Chiefs and senior diplomatic managers sit at administrative desks, distant from daily interviews, focusing on macro-level throughput, operational metrics, and diplomatic ties with corporate executives," she said.Administrative pressure to issue visasSiddiqui said the Chennai Consulate General at that time favoured principled adjudication but there was pressure from the highest level of the mission to increase the volume. " The consular chief in Delhi who oversaw all India missions, heavily focused on processing volume and managing bilateral commercial relations, routinely enforced a managerial culture of “issue, issue, issue," she added."When junior officers submitted formal fraud referrals regarding Cognizant, Satyam, TCS, and multinational corporate partners, senior managers repeatedly dismissed these concerns. Executive leadership routinely praised Cognizant and other corporate actors as “top-notch” entities without ever examining individual credentials with the rigor required at the window. As a result, corrupt HR managers and corporate entities operated a virtually unimpeded pipeline into the US labor market," Siddiqui said"Had leadership backed the officers on the line, taken our fraud referrals seriously, and dismantled corporate fast-track loopholes two decades ago, decades of systemic visa abuse, wage suppression, and immigration fraud could have been prevented. A stitch in time would have saved nine," she added.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

Regardless, that's who the ad was for — and it worked! THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! articles.title: In 1992, Rod Stewart sold his 1925 Los Angeles mansion for $6.25 million; after a two-year restoration and estate expansion, the nearly 6-acre compound sold in two deals totaling $86 million
articles.summary: Real Estate News: A historic 5.8-acre estate in Holmby Hills, which includes the former 1925 Spanish Colonial Revival mansion of rock star Rod Stewart, has sold in two .
articles.body: A historic 5.8-acre estate in Holmby Hills, which includes the former 1925 Spanish Colonial Revival mansion of rock star Rod Stewart, has sold in two separate deals totaling $86 million (£68 million). According to real estate records published by The Wall Street Journal and reported by Galerie Magazine, the combined sales end more than 30 years of ownership by daytime television executive producer Bradley Bell and his wife, former diplomat Colleen Bell. The couple bought the original house from Stewart in 1992 for $6.25 million. They then spent two years restoring the property while also buying nearby land, eventually creating a nearly six-acre estate in one of Los Angeles' most exclusive neighborhoods.Estate divided between two buyersInstead of selling the full 5.8-acre property to one buyer, the owners divided it into two separate parcels. The larger parcel covers about four acres and includes the main 17,000-square-foot mansion. It sold for $57 million to television, commercial and film producer David Zander. According to Galerie Magazine, Zander has previously bought and restored important historic homes, including Lasata, the historic Hamptons estate where Jacqueline Kennedy Onassis spent summers as a child. Real estate broker Drew Fenton of Carolwood Estates represented Zander, while Ben Bacal of Revel Real Estate represented the sellers. The second parcel covers about two acres and includes a historic cabin dating to around 1911. It sold for about $29 million to Nick Kaiser, co-founder of private equity firm Marlin Equity Partners.History and restorationThe main house has an important place in Southern California's architectural history. Retired distillery executive Henry Kern and his wife, Elsa Mary Kern, commissioned the home in 1925. Montecito architect George Washington Smith designed the mansion and was one of the early leaders of the Spanish Colonial Revival style. In The Legendary Estates of Beverly Hills, the late real estate historian Jeff Hyland wrote that the Kerns encouraged Smith to use much more detailed decoration than he normally preferred. Stewart bought the house in the 1970s and made several major design changes. These included adding marble floors and an Art Nouveau-style disco room. After buying the property in 1992, Bradley and Colleen Bell began a careful two-year restoration to remove those changes. They took out the marble flooring to uncover Smith's original hand-laid tile floors. They also removed later ceiling additions to reveal the historic carved coffered ceilings. Over the years, the couple continued to expand the property by buying nearby land. Some of that acreage came from their neighbor, actor Gregory Peck.Modern features across the expanded estateAfter the restoration and expansion, the property became a large private retreat that combines 1920s architecture with modern luxury features. The estate includes a 17,000-square-foot main house and a guest house, with a total of 13 bedrooms and 19 bathrooms.Major features across the house and grounds include:Brèche de Vendôme marble floors and two-story art gallery walls.A formal dining room that can seat 20 guests.A green wood-paneled speakeasy and private screening room.Two fully equipped gyms and a private tearoom.A motor court built around a large stone fountain.A resort-style swimming pool, spa and outdoor kitchen.A full-size professional soccer field on the landscaped grounds.The combined $86 million sale is one of the largest residential real estate transactions recorded in Los Angeles. It also highlights continued interest in large historic estates in prime Westside neighborhoods.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Bombing at mosque near police offices in Pakistan kills at least 21
articles.summary: PESHAWAR, Pakistan — A vehicle bomb exploded Friday at a mosque near police offices in northwestern Pakistan as gunmen tried to storm the compound in an attack that killed at least 21 people and wounded 80 others, police and rescue officials said.
articles.body: PESHAWAR, Pakistan — A vehicle bomb exploded Friday at a mosque near police offices in northwestern Pakistan as gunmen tried to storm the compound in an attack that killed at least 21 people and wounded 80 others, police and rescue officials said. Among those killed and wounded were police officers attending prayers at the mosque. The coordinated assault was the latest in a surge of militant violence near the border with Afghanistan where Pakistani Taliban militants have increasingly targeted police and other security forces as the government intensifies operations against them. The bombing occurred in Kohat, a district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. An attacker apparently rammed an explosives-laden vehicle into the mosque, said Zulfiqar Hameed, the provincial police chief. At least seven armed gunmen also attempted to enter the police compound and exchanged fire with officers. Six of the gunmen were killed, according to police, who said one suicide bomber attacked the nearby office of an intelligence agency. The police compound housed counter-terrorism police, who had carried out operations against militants across the province in recent years. Most of those killed were police officers, hospital officials said. Bilal Faizi, a senior rescue official, said most of the dead and wounded had been attending prayers at the mosque. Photos from the scene showed the outer wall of the police offices had collapsed and the mosque was badly damaged. Smoke rose over the site after the blast, which witnesses and residents said was heard far away, followed by gunfire. Inside the mosque, piles of bricks and concrete buried the floor, wires dangled from cracked walls and daylight poured through jagged holes in the roof, while a ceiling fan hung above the wreckage. Residents said the exchange of fire continued hours after the coordinated attack. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif condemned the attack and expressed sorrow over the casualties. He directed authorities to accelerate rescue operations. No group immediately claimed responsibility for the attack, but suspicion was likely to fall on the Pakistani Taliban, formally known as Tehrik-e-Taliban Pakistan, or TTP. The attack comes a day after a roadside bomb struck a security forces convoy in the northwestern Hangu district and killed six soldiers. Government troops also conducted raids in various areas Thursday and killed 10 militants believed to be members of the Pakistani Taliban, the military and police said. Pakistani Taliban have stepped up attacks on police and civilians in recent years. In 2023, a suicide bomber killed 101 people in an attack inside a mosque in Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province. The group is separate from but allied with Afghanistan’s Taliban, which returned to power in 2021. Pakistan often accuses Kabul of sheltering the TTP and turning a blind eye to cross-border militant attacks. The government in Kabul has denied the allegations. Tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan have remained high since Pakistan targeted alleged TTP hideouts in Afghanistan in 2025. The strikes triggered border clashes, prompting Qatar and Turkey to mediate a ceasefire. China later facilitated peace talks, but the two sides failed to reach an agreement. Friday’s bombing came a day after Turkey’s state-run Anadolu Agency reported Turkish intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin met with Sharif, the Pakistan army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir and intelligence chief Lt. Gen. Asim Malik. Kalin said Turkey would continue to make efforts to help resolve the tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan through dialogue, the news agency reported. The Turkish intelligence chief also met with the government in Afghanistan. Hamdullah Fitrat, deputy spokesperson for the Afghan Taliban, said Thursday that top officials in Kabul held talks with Kalin and a senior Qatari security official. The talks addressed tensions between Afghanistan and Pakistan.

articles.title: Nottingham attacks family condemn police chief's promotion
articles.summary: Police say the process consisted of an application form, a people panel and external advisors.
articles.body:
The father of a student who was stabbed to death in the Nottingham attacks has criticised a move by Nottinghamshire Police to promote the senior officer who led the investigation.

Grace O'Malley-Kumar, Barnaby Webber and Ian Coates were stabbed on 13 June 2023 by Valdo Calocane, leading to a public inquiry .

Rob Griffin, of Nottinghamshire Police, was temporary deputy chief constable from 29 April 2025 and was appointed substantively into the role following a selection process in August, the force said.

Sanjoy Kumar, Grace's dad, told the BBC on Friday: "I think this is completely wrong."

Police say the process consisted of an application form, a people panel and external advisors.

Griffin has previously been described by Barnaby's mother Emma Webber as having "blood on his hands" , following the force's failure to detain Calocane, who had been diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 2020, after an arrest warrant was issued in September 2022.

Kumar told the BBC Griffin had a "long history" with the Nottingham Inquiry , adding: "He also initially was going to go with a statement that the Nottinghamshire Police could not do any more to actually prevent the attacks, which we found really offensive when he admitted at the inquiry that a lot more could've been done.

"Furthermore, he didn't let us know about the professional standards investigations that were taking place."

Kumar said families would have expected people appointed in senior police roles, such as the deputy chief constable, to have "candour and integrity".

"We clearly felt that lacking in this case," he added.

He said he wanted to ask the secretary of state responsible for policing in the UK and the policing minister "what on earth is going on here?"

He added: "This is not someone who is reliable, this is someone who misled victims in a horrific situation.

"This is a person who lacked candour and integrity from our point of view. Why was he appointed to this role and made substantive from an active role?

"I think this is completely wrong, and the message it gives out to people in the country is that this government does nothing but reward failure."

A spokesperson for Nottinghamshire Police said: "Rob Griffin was temporary deputy chief constable of Nottinghamshire Police from 29 April 2025 and was appointed substantively into the role following a selection process on 13 August 2026.

"The selection process took place between 6 July 2026, when the position was advertised, and 13 August 2026, when the process was completed.

"This process consisted of an application form, a people panel, which involved representatives from our support networks, staff associations, and members from external stakeholders, including Independent Advisory Groups and the Youth Commission, and an executive interview, which included two independent panel members."

articles.body: Jasontheween has joined the viral “GGEZ” trend after connecting with Angelina Zhang, better known online as Sugar. The creator spoke with Sugar during his September 17 Twitch stream and later recreated the opening of the song with her. “GGEZ,” performed by Sugar and Kaien Nuen, has quickly spread across social media because of its gaming-inspired lyrics and Sugar’s memorable opening line. The song’s rise has also brought more attention to Sugar, who was already popular on Douyin, TikTok and Instagram. Now, fans are waiting to see whether the pair will take the collaboration further online.Jasontheween connects with GGEZ star Sugar during Twitch stream“GGEZ” became a viral internet song after its release in late August. The track is built around the gaming phrase “GG EZ,” short for “Good Game, Easy,” which players often use after winning a competitive match. The song is officially credited to Kaien Nuen, Sugar and M.Sasuke.Sugar quickly became one of the most recognizable parts of the track. She opens the music video with “GG ****ing EZ” before responding to Kaien Nuen with “**ggin EZ.” Her delivery helped turn the line into a memorable moment and led to people calling her the “GG EZ girl.”Angelina Zhang already had a following before the song took off. She was especially known for creating content on Douyin, the Chinese version of TikTok, while also building audiences on TikTok and Instagram. Her content has included music, cosplay and video game-focused e-girl culture.The song’s popularity eventually reached Jasontheween. The CORE Boys member first used the sound in a TikTok with his cameraman YBG. He then took things a step further during his September 17 livestream.Jason contacted Sugar on Discord while he was live on Twitch. The two later recreated the opening part of “GGEZ,” with Jason taking Kaien Nuen’s role while Sugar repeated her two well-known lines.Jasontheween’s September 17 stream also included “GGEZ” in its title, showing how closely the viral song had become connected to his content. Stream tracking data lists the broadcast at more than six hours, with the stream centered partly around the trend.Sugar reveals GGEZ was originally made with AIBefore recreating the song, Jasontheween asked Sugar about the sudden attention surrounding “GGEZ.” She explained that the reaction was very different from what she was used to because most of her previous work had been connected to Chinese social media.“It's very new to me because I'm not really from North American media. I don't know how you deal with this socially relevant stuff, but I've never been socially relevant.”Sugar also revealed an interesting detail about how the song started. According to her, the original version was AI-generated before she and Kaien Nuen created their own version with recorded tracks and lyrics.“It is [AI]. The original was... it was an AI-produced song, but for our version, we did all of the tracks and all of the lyrics.”The conversation then moved toward the possibility of another gaming-inspired track called “Good Luck Have Fun,” or “GLHF.” YBG suggested that people were already waiting for it.Sugar appeared surprised by the idea of making another song but did not completely rule it out.“Wait, you making another one?!..”YBG replied that he did not even know how to write songs, while Sugar added:“I don't know how to write songs... But if y'all tryin' to hop on the next remix, let me know.”For now, the “GGEZ” moment has given Sugar a new audience in North American creator circles. articles.title: Singing the Canadian National Anthem at the Buffalo Bills Home Opener was a mistake
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills had the band Barenaked Ladies sing "O Canada" at Highmark Stadium's inaugural opener despite no Canadian team being involved, sparking fan backlash.
articles.body: The Buffalo Bills inaugural regular season home opener couldn't have gone much better. The brand new Highmark Stadium was buzzing from hours before the game in the parking lot with fans crashing through foldable tables, to the final whistle in a convincing win over Detroit. The one stain on the night was how it started. The team decided to honor neighboring Canada by singing their national anthem. To many fans it felt strange and out of place to sing a foreign nation's anthem when there was no Canadian team involved in the game. I wholeheartedly agree. The Buffalo Bills have a longstanding relationship with the people north of the border. The team has a substantial footprint in Canada, with many fans making the short drive to attend Bills games for decades. The organization even had a 2026 draft pick announced from Canada on the broadcast. Bills owner Terry Pegula also owns the Buffalo Sabres, who sing "O Canada" before every home game, regardless if they are playing a Canada-based team. I still don't believe this was the right decision on Thursday night. SABRES FANS JUMP IN AS ANTHEM SINGER'S MIC CRAPS OUT DURING 'O, CANADA' While the Barenaked Ladies, a Canadian alternative rock band sung a subpar rendition of "O Canada", the broadcast showcased a massive Canadian flag on the field by one end zone and an American flag on the other. It felt odd to watch the inaugural regular season game of America's newest stadium, featuring American teams exclusively, go out of their way to honor a foreign nation. Honestly, it came across more like a marketing ploy and virtue signaling more than anything. I know I'm not alone in that sentiment. Many fans expressed confusion online, including Canadians, and even Fox News Contributor and US Marine Joey Jones scolded the decision. Jones said, "We play the [United States] National Anthem not to honor fans who enjoy entertainment, but to honor the men and women serving this country, providing freedom and security so we can do that during a time of war." FOX NEWS' JOHNNY 'JOEY' JONES REENLISTS IN UNITED STATES MARINE CORPS Jones went on to provide a history lesson to the Bills and the National Football League saying, "We play our national anthem because in 1918 we entered WWI, and they wanted to honor a Navy player that was out on the field. They wanted to honor that our sons and some daughters were fighting a war in trenches in some of the ugliest warfare every seen in our lives." Jones is exactly right. This isn't about not liking our neighbors to the north. It's not about refusing to be friendly. It's not about Trump. It's incredible to see so many Canadians enjoy our sports, but honoring their nation by singing their national anthem goes too far, especially when no Canadian teams are involved. You can honor the Canadian Bills fans and season ticket holders without honoring the nation as a whole. If the Bills wanted to give a special shoutout to Canadian fans pregame, thanking them for their support and dedication over the years, I'd have no problem with it, but going as far as honoring another nation, is borderline disrespectful to the history of our anthem and those that have fought and died to defend its rights and freedoms. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The funny and ironic aspect of all of this, is the fact that Ford Field (Lions stadium) is just as close to the Canadian border as Highmark Stadium is, yet they have never sung "O Canada" in order to "honor" their prominent Canadian fan base. I don't see this as much of a virtue signal as singing "Lift Every Voice," also known as the Black National Anthem, but it's a close second. When American teams are playing an American sport on American soil, we should stick to honoring our nation. America has one anthem and if foreign sports fans want to come over the border to enjoy these games, they are welcome, we're glad they're here, but they shouldn't expect or want us to honor their nation through songs of allegiance. The Bills are said to only perform the Canadian National Anthem for their home opener. Let's hope that is the case.

articles.title: US man claims he was fired just 2.5 hours into new job over 'hygiene issue' after 9 months of unemployment
articles.summary: US News: A New York man who had spent nearly 10 months looking for work says his new job lasted just 2.5 hours after a staffing agency told him he was being le.
articles.body: A New York man who had spent nearly 10 months looking for work says his new job lasted just 2.5 hours after a staffing agency told him he was being let go over alleged “hygiene issues”. The man, who uses the Reddit username Havocko, said he was left confused because he had showered, worn a brand-new shirt and believed he was well groomed on his first day. New York Post identified him as 35-year-old Chris Smalls. He also clarified in the comments that he is Black and not Indian, and the office was diverse.The man shared the experience in a post on Reddit's r/BoyDinnerDiaries sparking a discussion about what may have happened during his brief time at the workplace.According to his account, he had been unemployed for about nine and a half months and had already run out of unemployment benefits when he finally secured a new position through a temp agency. He said the job paid more than his previous one and appeared to be a good opportunity.I was let go from my new job after 2.5hrs. byu/Havocko inBoyDinnerDiariesThe night before starting, he said he took a shower and kept out a brand-new polo shirt for the following morning.His first few hours at the company initially appeared to go smoothly. A supervisor showed him around the new office, which he said had facilities he had not encountered at previous workplaces, including a stocked kitchen and bathroom.The supervisor explained the job and, around 10am, another employee took over his training.Things changed shortly afterwards.The supervisor told him he could take an early lunch before noon. She later called his trainer into a meeting. When the trainer returned, she told him she had other work to complete and asked him to sit there for the time being.The supervisor again told him to take an early lunch before noon.As he was leaving the building, however, the temp agency called him.He was told that his assignment was being terminated because of “hygiene issues”.The man said he was stunned by the explanation. In his Reddit post, he said he had showered before going to work, was well groomed and had deliberately worn a new polo shirt. He said that, at most, his trousers might have needed a lint roller.'I honestly don't know'The lack of a specific explanation appears to have been what troubled him most.In follow-up comments and in an interview with the New York Post, he said the staffing agency representative who informed him of the dismissal also appeared uncertain about what exactly had happened. He said she asked what he had been wearing but did not tell him what aspect of his hygiene had allegedly caused concern.The man then tried to work out whether there was something he had done during those first few hours that he was unaware of.He wondered whether an ordinary action, such as scratching his nose, might have been misinterpreted. He also questioned whether someone might have noticed him burping.“I honestly don't know,” he wrote, saying he had received no closure.He also asked people close to him whether they had noticed any unusual smell. According to his account, two friends told him they did not detect body odour.He said he brushes and flosses regularly and had visited a dentist during the summer. He also said he lives with a particularly clean roommate and keeps his home clean despite having a cat and a dog.Reddit users debate what happenedThe post prompted a range of reactions online.Some Reddit users suggested that the stated reason might not have been the real reason for the dismissal, while others said it was possible the man had an odour he was unaware of.The man also said the experience was particularly difficult because he had spent months trying to find employment and had been looking forward to starting the new job.According to the New York Post, he has not been offered another assignment by the staffing agency and said he had not yet been paid for the short period he worked.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Ponzi schemer who defrauded Travis Kelce tried to marry U.S. citizen to avoid deportation, prosecutors say
articles.summary: The undocumented Indian immigrant behind a multi-million dollar Ponzi scheme tried to marry an American citizen before he was sentenced to 11 years in prison, court records show.
articles.body: The undocumented Indian immigrant behind a multi-million dollar Ponzi scheme that defrauded Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce and other investors tried to marry an American citizen before he was sentenced this week to 11 years in prison, court records show. Federal prosecutors opposed Siddharth Jawahar’s request to marry Caroline Tredway, saying he may be an attempting “to obtain immigration status in the United States,” according to a Sept. 4 filing in the U.S. District Court for Eastern District of Missouri. Jawahar’s lawyer, however, insisted his client was not engaging in “marriage fraud” and said Tredway was willing to buy a $25 wedding ring and spend another $75 on an “officiant” to perform the ceremony. “The truth is, Mr. Jawahar very much hopes to stay here after his sentence and build a life with Caroline, and he plans to pursue any legal avenues to do so,” attorney Doug Passon stated his Sept. 13 response. Passon also acknowledged both Jawahar and Tredway are aware that “given this case and his current immigration status, his ability to remain here is highly unlikely.” The revelations came two days after the 38-year-old Indian national, who pleaded guilty to three counts of wire fraud in January, was sentenced to prison and ordered to repay $31 million in restitution to victims he defrauded from 2016 to 2023. It was during this proceeding at the U.S. District Court in St. Louis that a prosecutor briefly mentioned that Kelce was one of Jawahar’s many high-profile victims. Kelce has not addressed the report publicly. NBC reached out to Tredway, who lives near Cleveland, to find out if she and Jawahar are still intending to marry. She has not responded. “I don’t have any comment on that, and find it wholly irrelevant to the issues at hand,” Passon said in an emailed response to NBC News. But in a June 30, 2026 phone call that was monitored by the authorities, Jawahar and Tredway discussed the implications of them getting married, court records revealed. “What if you get deported?” Tredway asked. “If you don’t marry me, I guess that might happen,” Jawahar replied. During that same conversation, the records showed, Jawahar also told Tredway that “the chance of me getting deported goes down dramatically” if they tied the knot. Tredway, in an August letter to the court, said they met in 2021 and “officially became romantic” in February 2023. “That night, Sid voiced his interest in me and asked me out on a date for the next evening,” she wrote. “That date turned out to be the best date of both of our lives. Because we already had such a strong foundation of trust and friendship, we fell deeply in love very quickly.” Tredway, in her letter, insisted that “legitimizing our marriage before he enters a federal facility is vital for our family.” “I enter into this marriage with my eyes completely open to Sid’s legal situation,” Tredway wrote. In subsequent conversations with Tredway’s relatives, Jawahar also said he expected be sentenced to “close to time served” and that he would then “focus on getting a pardon because there were a lot of gross violations of the law.” “But my move after that is — I’d most likely be teaching a class in business ethics at Fordham University,” he was recorded as saying. Marrying a U.S. citizen was apparently not the only gambit by Jawahar to avoid a lengthy prison sentence. Jawahar in August, according to prosecutors, paid a prominent Missouri political consulting firm called Axiom $10,000 to try and sway the judge presiding over the case by getting U.S. Rep. Sam Graves, a Missouri Republican, to write a letter of support on his behalf. Axiom also engineered the publication of a favorable article about Jawahar in a local newspaper that did not mention he was awaiting sentencing for a scheme that resulted in what U.S. District Judge Zachary Bluestone called “enormous losses” for investors. Jawahar also tried to coach a victim to give a favorable statement to authorities and sought to have his sister wipe his iPhone, prosecutors said. Much of Jawahar’s past remains murky, but records show that he arrived in the U.S. from India around the time he began studying at the University of Texas in fall 2005. Jawahar was a government and philosophy major and took classes as recently as spring 2012 but did not graduate with a degree, a spokesperson at the school said. The U.S. attorney’s office, however, says Jawahar ran a Texas-based investment company called Swiftarc Capital LLC and carried out a classic Ponzi scheme, using money from new investors to repay older investors and to fuel an extravagant lifestyle. Jawahar traveled on private jets, stayed at luxury hotels, went on spending sprees and had memberships at private clubs across the U.S. From July 2016 to December 2023, Jawahar’s company took in more than $35 million but invested roughly $10 million, the prosecutor’s office said. In addition to Kelce, Jawahar was reportedly able to lure other top athletes to invest in his venture capital fund. That group, according to a Forbes article published Jun 14, 2021, included NBA players Gary Harris, Tim Hardaway Jr. and Mason Plumlee. “I’m thankful for Sid bringing me in, taking me under his wing and believing in me,” Harris was quoted as saying of Jawahar. NBC News reached out to their agents asking whether the NBA players lost any money as a result of their investing with Jawahar and whether they cooperated with the federal investigation. There was no response from their agents.

articles.title: In 2004, Ken Griffey Jr. paid $2.575 million for 11.58 lakefront acres near Orlando; four years later he completed a 22,108-sq-ft custom mansion, and the estate is now listed for $27 million
articles.summary: US News: Baseball Hall of Famer Ken Griffey Jr. has listed his custom-built lakefront mansion near Orlando for $27 million (£21.2 million), putting a price on .
articles.body: Baseball Hall of Famer Ken Griffey Jr. has listed his custom-built lakefront mansion near Orlando for $27 million (£21.2 million), putting a price on a property he has owned for more than 20 years. The 13-time Major League Baseball All-Star bought the 11.58-acre site on Cypress Lake in 2004 for $2.575 million, according to Orange County property records cited by Mansion Global and Orlando Weekly. After buying the undeveloped land, the former Seattle Mariners and Cincinnati Reds outfielder spent four years designing and building a huge 22,108-square-foot Mediterranean-style home. Construction was completed in 2008. Located at 5603 Marleon Drive in the gated community of Windermere, the estate has more than 440 feet of direct shoreline along the Butler Chain of Lakes. The $27 million asking price is more than 10 times what Griffey paid for the land 22 years ago.Large scale and detailed designThe property is entered through a security gate that leads to a circular driveway and a covered entrance surrounded by stone columns and turret-style wings. Inside, a 28-foot-high grand foyer features high ceilings and a double staircase with custom ironwork. The home is divided into several living areas, combining formal rooms for entertaining with private spaces for the family. According to listing information from Premier Sotheby's International Realty and Realtor.com, the main house has seven bedrooms and 10 bathrooms, including eight full bathrooms and two half-baths. The interior has a large gourmet kitchen with two islands, custom cabinets, a commercial-grade stove and a hidden pantry nearby. The main living spaces feature detailed wooden ceiling beams, stone fireplaces and floor-to-ceiling glass doors that open onto outdoor loggias. The property also has a separate guest wing with two bedrooms, its own living room and a private outside entrance for staff or visiting family members.Sports and luxury amenitiesBuilt while Griffey was at the height of his baseball career, the home was designed with custom entertainment and sports features across its three floors.Indoor amenities include:A modern private movie theater with tiered leather seats.An indoor golf simulator and several game rooms.A glass-enclosed, climate-controlled wine tasting room.A fully equipped commercial-style gym and sauna.A private elevator serving all three floors.The outdoor grounds are designed like a private resort. At the back of the home is a 125,000-gallon saltwater pool with rock waterfalls, a built-in water slide, a diving board and an attached spa. Other features across the 11.58-acre property include a full-size private basketball court, a covered outdoor kitchen, a large boat dock and a 10-car garage with vehicle lifts.Luxury community on the Butler ChainThe estate is in Windermere, a suburb that has long attracted professional athletes, business executives and celebrities because of its privacy, location near Orlando and access to the connected Butler Chain of Lakes. Listing agent Llin Lu of Premier Sotheby's International Realty is handling the sale. The property is among the most expensive homes currently listed in Orange County. In addition to the private dock, the estate has access to a private boat ramp, giving residents direct access to Cypress Lake and the larger network of waterways. Griffey was inducted into the National Baseball Hall of Fame in 2016 after receiving a record 99.3 per cent of the vote. He lived at the property during the later part of his playing career and after retirement. The sale comes as his children have grown up, bringing an end to the baseball star's 22-year chapter in Central Florida.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Hasan Piker calls Bin Laden a ‘spoiled brat,’ labels 9/11 ‘blowback’ in Axios interview
articles.summary: Hasan Piker called Osama bin Laden a "spoiled brat" and labeled 9/11 as blowback for U.S. foreign policy in the Middle East and Afghanistan.
articles.body: Hasan Piker, the internet streamer and YouTube personality known for his progressive commentary, called Osama bin Laden a "spoiled brat" for his reasoning in orchestrating the Sept. 11, 2001 attacks, which he called "blowback" for U.S. actions in the Middle East in the preceding years. Speaking with Axios, Piker discussed bin Laden's remarks about why he targeted the United States: U.S. support of Israel, American oil policies and U.S. bases in the Middle East. He noted that bin Laden was once a U.S. ally when the U.S. trained, funded, and armed the mujahideen in Afghanistan during the Soviet-Afghan War. "The action was so heinous and so violent that — and also … given his position as formerly an American ally … I think that he came across a little bit more as a spoiled brat that wasn't getting his way. With many backers in the Saudi kingdom as well, and the royal family," Piker said. CLINTON, BUSH RECEIVED MULTIPLE WARNINGS ON BIN LADEN HIJACK PLOTS BEFORE 9/11, DECLASSIFIED FILES SHOW The left-wing streamer said he wants fewer actors like bin Laden to "exist in general." "The other path of least resistance is to not interfere in these affairs in general and not continue to dominate and create an environment where people are going to seek out revenge and put us in a position of danger," he said. RADICAL EL-SAYED ALLY DOUBLES DOWN ON ANTI-AMERICAN RHETORIC WITH STUNNING TERRORIST COMPARISON Piker called the Sept. 11 attacks a "horrifying tragedy" and called them blowback for U.S. actions in the Middle East. "Blowback is not a justification. Blowback is just what it is," he said. "A justification offers either a moral condemnation or a moral acceptance of the act. I do not accept the act of 9/11 morally". HASAN PIKER INSISTS MIDDLE EAST WOULD BE 'MORE STABLE' IF IRAN HAD NUCLEAR WEAPONS DURING AXIOS INTERVIEW GOT A TIP? Piker has faced backlash for remarks in the same interview where he compared the United States to al-Qaeda "pound for pound". articles.title: 73-year-old Indian-origin California 'healer' accused of sexually assaulting 4 clients; attorney says he's an acupressure practitioner
articles.summary: US News: A 73-year-old California man who had built a reputation as a “healer” in the local Sikh community has been accused of sexually assaulting four clients.
articles.body: A 73-year-old California man who had built a reputation as a “healer” in the local Sikh community has been accused of sexually assaulting four clients during treatment sessions at his Selma home, according to police and court records.Pal Singh was arrested by the Selma Police Department on September 8 and faces four felony counts of sexual assault. The allegations involve four separate victims and incidents that allegedly occurred between June 2023 and July 2025, according to court records obtained by ABC30.Police said Singh was operating what authorities described as an unlicensed chiropractic practice from his home, where he provided treatment services to clients.Investigators said Singh was known within the Sikh community as a “healer” and had developed a following that extended beyond Selma. People reportedly travelled from other parts of California to seek his services, with online reviews indicating that some clients travelled long distances for appointments. One reviewer said they had travelled from Canada for treatment, ABC30 reported.What police allegedAccording to Selma police, investigators began after receiving complaints from clients about inappropriate touching at his residence.“We had multiple complaints from clients about inappropriate touching that was going on at the location, and we were finally able to make an arrest in that case,” Selma Police Commander Tim Cannon told ABC30.The four criminal charges relate to alleged incidents involving four separate victims. Investigators said the alleged assaults occurred during treatment appointments.Police have not publicly detailed what medical or healing problem each person had sought treatment for.Cannon said authorities believe there could be additional victims who have not yet contacted police. Investigators also believe some potential victims could live outside Fresno County because people travelled to Selma to receive treatment from Singh.“We've had allegations for several years,” Cannon said, adding that investigators had also received secondhand information about possible additional victims who had not come forward.Singh described himself as an acupressure practitionerCourt documents filed by Singh's attorney, Eddie Ruiz, said Singh became a Sikh priest while living in India in his mid-20s and continued his religious work after moving to Selma. A character letter submitted to the court said he served as a priest at the Sikh Center of the Pacific Coast in Selma between 2010 and 2016.Ruiz wrote that Singh later moved into acupressure, receiving training in India and then completing additional online training after moving to California.Neighbors told ABC30 that they regularly saw families arriving at Singh's residence for appointments.His social media accounts also featured photographs and videos of people who had sought his services, while online reviews indicated that his clients came from outside the immediate area.Released on bailSingh was released after posting bail several days after his arrest.In court filings seeking his release, his attorney said Singh wanted to continue working, support his family and assist with his defence.Singh has pleaded not guilty to all four charges. His next court appearance is scheduled for October 27.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ironmouse’s Fortnite ‘Cry For Me’ emote sparks AI debate: Why are her past comments resurfacing now?
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Twitch star Ironmouse is facing criticism after Fortnite revealed her “Cry For Me” emote, with some X users questioning how the collaboration fits wit.
articles.body: Twitch star Ironmouse is facing criticism after Fortnite revealed her “Cry For Me” emote, with some X users questioning how the collaboration fits with her earlier comments about generative AI. The VTuber has previously spoken strongly against working with AI companies and pulled out of a sponsored collaboration with Neverness to Everness after raising concerns about its use of generative AI. Fortnite, however, has publicly introduced AI-powered tools for creators and NPCs. The latest collaboration has therefore brought Ironmouse’s past comments back into the discussion, while streamer Tectone has also joined the online criticism.Ironmouse’s past comments on AI return after Fortnite collaborationIronmouse has been open about her opposition to generative AI. During a March 2026 livestream, she spoke about receiving repeated sponsorship offers from AI companies.The VTuber said she was not interested in working with them and questioned why they continued contacting her despite her position.“Oh, my god! Talking about AI, this AI company keeps ****** messaging me. This AI company keeps messaging me, asking to do, like, they keep asking to do, like, a sponsor partnership with me. And, like, I've just been ignoring them, but they keep on messaging me over and over again. And I just want to be like, ‘**** off, mate! Oi, mate, **** off! **** off, mate!’ It's multiple AI stuff. One of them is a chatbot. The other one is an AI music thing. AI to create AI music, and it's just like mate, what the ****? Like, I'm the wrong person to talk to. Like, you ******* messaged the wrong person, bro!”Her position became a bigger topic in May when she ended her involvement with Neverness to Everness. Ironmouse said her team had been told the game would not contain generative AI. After players raised concerns about suspected AI-created assets, she said she would no longer play or promote the game.The situation later became more complicated when Hotta Studio said AI-assisted tools had been used on a small number of background and environmental assets. The developer also said those assets would be reviewed and reworked.Fortnite now has documented AI features of its own. Epic Games introduced AI-powered conversations for Fortnite creators in 2026. The company said developers could use the system to create NPCs that respond to players with unscripted dialogue.That difference is what some users focused on after Fortnite announced its collaboration with Ironmouse.X users and Tectone question Ironmouse’s Fortnite dealOn September 17, 2026, X user @HYPEX shared the “Cry For Me” emote connected to Ironmouse. The post quickly drew attention online and brought her previous AI comments back into the conversation.Some users accused the VTuber of having different standards for different games. X user @Pirat_Nation questioned why Ironmouse had rejected Neverness to Everness over AI concerns while appearing excited about Fortnite.YouTuber Rev Says Desu also questioned the collaboration, writing:“Ironmouse, who will ‘never support games with ai’, when she’s offered a paid sponsorship with a game that openly uses generative ai:”Another X user, @DejaWukong, wrote:“remember that time ironmouse said she would never support or play a game with ai. Money over morals I guess”These posts represent the criticism from individual users and do not establish why Ironmouse agreed to the Fortnite collaboration. Some online users have also pointed out that Fortnite’s AI use and the Neverness to Everness controversy are not necessarily identical situations. In the NTE case, Ironmouse’s dispute centered partly on what she and her team were told about AI use before the collaboration.Streamer John “Tectone” also commented on the situation. He claimed that Ironmouse would not respond to the criticism and accused her supporters of attacking people who questioned her position.“She won’t address anything. She never does, because every time she has it’s made her look far worse. So she’ll do the age old tactic, say nothing and let her rabid ****** fanbase defend her. Not by debunking any claims, not by providing proof of misinformation. Just slandering anyone who tells the truth about mouse. Once you understand how people like this work, you’ll never unsee it.”As of September 18, Ironmouse had not publicly addressed the latest criticism. Meanwhile, the Fortnite collaboration continues to attract attention from both her supporters and users questioning how it fits with her earlier position on generative AI.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
